frontend-viewmodels:symbol:frontend/src/.reason: the Community tab's donations list (Buy Me a Coffee)

app.text: A personal website and admin console, built as a frontend, an ASP.NET Core minimal API and a PostgreSQL database. The frontend is feature modules: public pages (About Me, Apps, YouTube, Contact, Updates, Terms, Support) and admin-only tabs (Settings, Notifications, Analytics, Meetings, Feature Testing), with Redux holding auth state. The backend has one folder per feature with its own endpoints, validation and EF Core entities, plus background workers for alerts, emails, meeting reminders and YouTube refresh. Admin sessions are cookies backed by admin_sessions. PostgreSQL stores editable pages as JSON documents, external data as cached snapshots, and contacts, meetings, subscribers, visits and alerts as ordinary rows.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.CachePrefix.text: Builds the Redis key prefix "portfolio:{database}:" from the Postgres connection string's database name, so APIs on different databases sharing one Redis don't collide. Used by Program at startup.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.AboutPa.text: EF entity for the single-row About Me page, stored as one JSON document in the about_page table. Read and written whole by AboutEndpoints and ResumeEndpoints, and mapped in PortfolioDbContext.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.AdminSe.text: EF entity for a signed-in admin device, stored in admin_sessions with only the SHA-256 hash of the cookie token, plus idle and absolute expiry times. Created and removed by AdminSessionService in the auth feature.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.AlertCh.text: EF entity holding the on/off flag for each alert channel (ntfy, site notifications) in alert_channels; a missing row means enabled. Set from the Notifications tab via PushEndpoints and read by AlertPreferences.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.AlertPr.text: Stores whether each kind of phone alert is switched on in the Notifications tab. A kind with no row counts as on. Used by the alerts feature and the notifications endpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.Announc.text: Tracks an app or video the subscribers may be emailed about, so nothing is announced twice. New apps wait for the admin's send or ignore decision, while new videos are approved at once. Written by the updates feature.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.AppCate.text: An admin-defined kind of app, such as 'Video game'. Categories are listed by their position and shown on apps. Managed by the apps endpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.AppEntr.text: An app shown on the Apps page, with its media, categories, platforms, store links, and admin-set order. Used by the apps endpoints, file cleanup, and the updates feature for announcements and What's new.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.Contact.text: The first message in a contact conversation, from the public form or an email to the site's address. The admin answers by email, and the conversation is tracked by read state and last activity. Used by the contact and meetings endpoints.
A follow-up message in a contact conversation: either the admin's emailed answer or the visitor's emailed reply. Linked to its ContactMessage and managed by the contact endpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.Donatio.text: A payment event from Buy Me a Coffee's webhook, such as a donation, membership, or refund, stored once per event. Test payments are flagged, and the payer's email is visible only to the admin. Used by the support endpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.LeetCod.text: The last LeetCode stats fetched for a username, kept so they survive restarts and can still be shown when LeetCode is unreachable. Written by LeetCodeStatsService.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.Meeting.text: A Cal.com booking, kept in sync through its webhook, with a status and a decision token for accepting or declining from the phone alert. Used by the meetings reminders and endpoints, and by the contact endpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.PhoneAl.text: A history of phone alerts the site raised, whether sent, skipped, or failed, with the channels used. Written by AlertWorker and shown on the Notifications tab.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.Portfol.text: The Entity Framework database context that maps the app's tables (profile, admin sessions, contact messages, apps, alerts, subscribers, snapshots, and more) and seeds the default profile. Most feature services and endpoints read and write through it.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.Profile.text: The single stored profile row that holds the site owner's first name, seeded with id 1. Read and updated by ProfileEndpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.PushDev.text: A browser or phone registered for site notifications, storing its push-service endpoint and encryption keys. PushEndpoints adds it, and WebPushSender uses it to deliver alerts.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.ResumeS.text: The single row holding the admin's résumé choices, private contact details, and the generated public and private PDFs. Only ResumeEndpoints uses it, and the phone number never appears in public data.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.SiteSet.text: A saved configuration override, such as the Resend API key, that takes precedence over app configuration. Secrets are stored encrypted. SettingsStore reads it and SettingsEndpoints manages it.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.SiteSta.text: The single row controlling which pages and features visitors see and whether maintenance mode is on, with its message. Edited in the Settings tab and read by SiteEndpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.StoredF.text: An uploaded file, such as the About Me photo or résumé, kept in the database. It is accessed through IFileStorage, so storage could move later. DatabaseFileStorage implements that access.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.Subscri.text: A person subscribed to update emails, added only after double opt-in confirmation and removed on unsubscribe. Used by the updates endpoints, the announcer, and announcement decisions.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.TermsPa.text: The single row holding the terms and conditions as one JSON document, read and saved as a whole. TermsEndpoints is its only user.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.UpdateE.text: The single row holding the wording of subscriber update emails as one JSON document, with defaults applying until the admin saves. UpdateEmailsEndpoints reads and writes it.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.Updates.text: A single-row record of when update announcements started. Only apps and videos posted after that time are announced, so new subscribers don't get the older backlog. Used by the updates announcer.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.VisitEv.text: One event within a visit, such as a page open, click, or error, with its page, optional label, and JSON detail. A per-visit sequence number orders events and makes resent batches harmless. Belongs to a VisitSession.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.VisitSe.text: One browser-tab visit, with a daily-salted visitor hash, entry page, referrer, UTM tags, device, country, theme, and counts. Owns its VisitEvents. The signed-in admin is never recorded.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.WebPush.text: The site's single VAPID key pair for Web Push, generated on first need and kept permanently so subscribed devices keep working. Used by the push sender and push endpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.WorkWit.text: The admin-set hourly rate for the Work with me page, stored as a currency code and amount. A default applies until the admin first saves a price. Used by the Work with me endpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Data.YouTube.text: A cached list of a channel's videos, newest first, stored as JSON with a fetch time. It survives restarts and can be shown when YouTube is unreachable. Written by the YouTube video store.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Abo.text: Placeholder content for the About Me page, covering colours, places, skills, experience, education, and more. It is served until the admin first saves the page. Used by the About endpoints and the JSON reader.

Public GET and admin-only PUT for the /about route. GET returns the stored page or the defaults; PUT validates, normalises, and saves the whole page, then deletes uploaded files it no longer uses. Resume and LeetCode endpoints depend on it.

Reads and writes the stored About page, upgrading older saved shapes on read, such as plain-text qualifications, skill levels, and company names. This avoids a data migration. Used by the About endpoints and the resume.

Validates and normalises the About page, returning errors keyed by JSON path (e.g. experience[0].title) so the editor can show each one beside its field. Other features' rules, including apps, resume, terms, and update emails, also use it.
The allowed language proficiency levels for the About section, from native down to beginner. AboutRules uses it to validate language entries.
The allowed licence categories for the About section: driving, flying, boating, and other. AboutRules uses it to validate licence entries.
The IDs of the three NeetCode problem lists (Blind 75, NeetCode 150, NeetCode 250), in display order. AboutRules and the resume document use them.
The allowed ways a person relates to a place: worked, studied, or visited. AboutDefaults, AboutRules, and the resume document use it.
The allowed purposes for a skill: work, academic, or personal. AboutDefaults and AboutRules use it to set defaults and validate skill entries.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Ale.text: The two ways alerts are delivered: the ntfy app and the site's own Web Push. Each can be switched on or off in the Notifications tab. AlertWorker and PushEndpoints use it.
The registry of every alert type the site sends to the admin's phone, grouped by category. Each can be switched off in Notifications, and new alert types are added here. Many features use it.
The Alerts config section holding the ntfy server, topic, and optional access token. Alerts are sent through ntfy; until a topic is set, they are only written to the log.

An in-memory cache of which alert kinds and channels are switched off. It loads from the database at startup and after each Notifications change, so the alert worker never waits on the database. AlertWorker, PushEndpoints, and NotificationsEndpoints use it.
The outcomes an alert can have in its history: sent, off, not-set-up, failed, or no-channel. AlertWorker records one for each alert.

Background service that drains the phone-alert queue one at a time, skips kinds switched off, sends each over every enabled channel (ntfy, web push), and writes the outcome to PhoneAlertLog. Prunes history older than 90 days hourly.

Exception handler for unhandled API exceptions, excluding cancellations and bad requests. It logs the error and queues a throttled API crash phone alert, at most once per hour per exception type and endpoint. The 500 response is left to the default handler.
Admin-only /notifications endpoints behind the Notifications tab: list alert kinds with on/off state and recent counts, toggle a kind, and page through the alert history, optionally filtered by kind.
Posts an alert as JSON to an ntfy server using the configured topic and optional bearer token, with a click link and action buttons. Only logs if no topic is set, and throws on HTTP failure.
In-memory alert queue, bounded at 100 with the oldest dropped, that AlertWorker reads from. SendThrottled allows one alert per key per hour and at most 10 throttled alerts per hour overall.

Admin-only /notifications endpoints for the alert channels (ntfy, browser push) on/off, plus managing browser push devices: fetch the site's VAPID public key, add or update a device, remove one, and send a test notification to it.

Configuration section (Site) holding the public URL used in alert and email links, the admin's time zone for alert times, and whether unfinished pages show by default. Used by notification senders, meetings, updates, and settings code.

Sends alerts as Web Push notifications to every registered browser device, encrypted and signed with the site's VAPID key pair, which is created once and stored. Removes devices whose push service returns 404 or 410.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Ana.text: Public endpoint that stores batches of visitors' browser events (rate-limited, always 204, skipping admins and bots), plus admin-only endpoints for the Engagement tab to read summaries, browse sessions, and delete them.

Background service that runs at startup and then daily, deleting visit sessions (and their events via cascade) whose last activity is older than the retention period of VisitRetentionMonths months from the terms.

Defines what the visitor tracker accepts and how it cleans events: known event types, length caps, and trimming instead of rejecting. Also parses referrers, UTM tags, countries and User-Agents for AnalyticsEndpoints and admin sessions.

Hashes each visitor's IP and User-Agent into an ID that stays stable within a UTC day. The salt lives only in memory and changes daily, so stored IDs can't be reversed to IPs. Used by AnalyticsEndpoints; restarts reset it.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.App.text: Routes for the apps section: public listing, categories and What's new, plus admin-only create, edit, delete and ordering. Reads and writes apps in the database, validates with AppRules, cleans up unused files, and proposes subscriber emails for new apps.
The three allowed media kinds for an app: image, video, and YouTube link. AppRules checks media entries against this list; AppEndpoints, UpdatesAnnouncer and FileEndpoints also rely on it.

Validates app and category submissions (title, description, media, categories, platforms, links), returning errors keyed by field path. Used by AppEndpoints on create, update and category saves; it relies on the YouTube and file-link helpers.

Recognises YouTube video links in common URL forms and extracts the 11-character video ID, or returns null for anything else. Used by AppRules to validate YouTube media and by AppEndpoints. Mirrors the frontend's media rules.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Aut.text: Admin access settings, bound from the Auth config section: which Google accounts may sign in (by email, optionally by permanent Google ID), plus the idle timeout (10 minutes) and maximum session length (12 hours). Read by auth code and by the contact, meetings and settings endpoints.

Manages the admin's sign-in sessions, one per device: creates them at sign-in, checks and extends them on each request, and lists or ends them. Stores only a hash of each cookie token in the database. Used by the auth setup, Google sign-in and auth endpoints.

Routes for admin sign-in and sessions: starts Google login, reports the current user and time left, signs out this device, and lets an admin list and end sessions on other devices. Redirects only to safe same-site paths. Built on AdminSessionService and GoogleSignIn.

Wires up admin authentication at startup: the session cookie (name and security set per environment), Google as the sign-in provider when credentials are configured, and per-request checks against AdminSessionService and AdminOptions. Called from Program; also used by GoogleSignIn and PushEndpoints.

Finishes Google sign-in: lets in only the admin account with a verified email, starting a cookie session on that device. Every sign-in and refusal sends a phone alert via IPhoneAlerts, with device and IP details.

Middleware that rejects state-changing requests (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) carrying the admin cookie when their Origin header is from another site, returning 403. Registered in the app pipeline as a second guard beside SameSite=Lax.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Con.text: Maps the /contact routes: a rate-limited public form, an inbound-email webhook, and admin-only inbox endpoints to list, read, mark read, delete and reply to messages. Uses PortfolioDbContext, sends phone alerts, and emails replies via Resend.

Validation for the contact form: name, email, message length (100–1000 characters after trimming) and topic. The frontend mirrors these rules in ContactForm.tsx; the server's checks are the ones that count, reused by resume, settings and updates.

Webhook for emails sent to the site's address, received through Resend: verifies the Svix signature, drops emails not addressed to the site, DMARC-failing or automatic ones, then adds each to the sender's latest conversation or starts one in the contact inbox.

Fetches a received email from Resend's API (GET /emails/receiving/{id}) with the configured key, and turns it into a ReceivedEmail, flagging automatic mail and carrying DMARC results. Used by InboundEmail; failures become ServiceException.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Fil.text: Implements IFileStorage by storing file bytes as rows in the stored_files table: save, fetch by id, and delete files that are older than a cutoff and not in a keep list. Suited to small files like photos and PDFs, not large media.

Deletes uploaded files that no About page or app references, once they're over a day old, so an open editor doesn't lose them. Called after saving About or app data; reads AboutContent and app media to collect the URLs still in use.

Maps the /files routes: admin-only uploads for photos, papers (PDF) and app images or videos, which get re-encoded or validated, plus a public GET that serves a stored file by id. Stores through IFileStorage; image processing lives in FileRules.

Upload rules: size caps (15 MB for photos and app images, 200 MB for papers and videos), and PreparePhotoAsync, which re-encodes a JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF as upright WebP with metadata stripped, scaled to fit pixel limits.
Thrown when an uploaded file isn't a picture that PreparePhotoAsync can process. Raised by FileRules and surfaced to the client through FileEndpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Lee.text: Fetches a user's public LeetCode stats from LeetCode's unofficial GraphQL endpoint and parses the answer into LeetCodeStats. Used by LeetCodeStatsService; it has no API key and may break if LeetCode changes its API.

Exposes a public GET /leetcode route that returns stats for the username set on the About Me page only. Responds 204 if none is set, 404 if the user is unknown, or 503 if LeetCode is unreachable with nothing saved.

In-memory, per-username cache of LeetCode lookups with expiry times, registered as a singleton and cleared on restart. It also holds a semaphore so concurrent requests trigger only one LeetCode call. Used by LeetCodeStatsService.

Returns LeetCode stats through three layers: memory cache, then the leetcode_stats database table, then LeetCode itself. Refreshes after 24 hours, and on failure shows saved stats and retries after 15 minutes. Used by LeetCodeEndpoints and ResumeEndpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Mee.text: HTTP client for Cal.com API v2, used to confirm, decline, and cancel bookings and to check the configured account. Authenticates with the API key from CalOptions and pins the cal-api-version header. Errors are reported as ServiceException.
The "Cal" configuration section, holding the booking link, Cal.com API key, and webhook secret, editable in the Settings tab. Provides the normalized public booking URL and validates link input.

Finds accepted meetings starting within the next day and sends phone alerts at 1 day, 2 hours, 5 minutes, and at start time, each only once. Only the latest due reminder is sent, and a missed start reminder still goes out within 10 minutes. Uses IPhoneAlerts and the meetings table.
Background service that runs MeetingReminders.SendDueAsync every 30 seconds in a fresh DI scope. Logs errors without stopping the loop.

Admin routes for invitation-only Cal.com meetings. A signed Cal.com webhook saves each booking and sends phone alerts. The admin lists, cancels, and gets the booking link, and accepts or declines requests, either signed in or via a phone-alert token.
Constant string values for a meeting's lifecycle: requested, accepted, declined, and cancelled. Used by MeetingReminders, MeetingsEndpoints, and ContactEndpoints.

Builds the admin's personal emails: replies to contact messages and notes about meeting decisions. Formats greetings, quoted originals, and meeting times in the attendee's time zone. Used by MeetingReminders, MeetingsEndpoints, and ContactEndpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Pla.text: In-memory search over about 170k world places with 1,000+ people, loaded lazily from an embedded gzipped file. Matches names by prefix, ignoring case and accents, largest first; text after a comma narrows by region or country. Serves PlaceEndpoints.
Admin-only GET /places/search endpoint used while adding places to the 'Where I've been' map. Delegates to CityIndex and returns up to the requested number of matches as City records.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Pro.text: Public, read-only endpoint returning the owner's first name from the Profile table, or 404 if none is set. Reads through PortfolioDbContext and is also exercised from the Portfolio.Api.http request file.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Res.text: Builds the About Me page as an A4 PDF résumé with QuestPDF, in a fixed section order and skipping empty sections. Name and contact details appear on the first page, with email and phone only in the private version. Called by ResumeEndpoints during generation.

Routes for the résumé: public PDF and headline, and admin-only settings, contact and section saves, and generation. Generation builds two PDFs (public without email/phone, private with them), stores them in ResumeSettings, and reads About Me data plus LeetCode stats.

Validation and normalization for résumé contact details, headline, and section and skill choices. Checks phone format and length, email validity, and that sections come from the known list. Used by ResumeEndpoints and PortfolioDbContext.

Constants for the About Me parts a résumé can include, in print order, plus the default set recruiters see (excluding map, LeetCode, and licences). Used by ResumeDocument, ResumeEndpoints, and ResumeRules.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Set.text: A simple exception for when a service refuses a request, carrying a message that is safe to show the admin. Thrown by the Cal.com, email, contact inbox, and update services.

Lists the settings the Settings tab can edit, each with a label, a secret flag, and validation rules for URLs, sender addresses, Cal.com links and ntfy topics. Used by SettingsEndpoints, and validation calls ContactRules and CalOptions.
Gives IOptionsMonitor<T> the SettingsStore's change token, so options bound from the Settings tab recompute when a setting is saved. Used by SettingsOptionsExtensions.

Admin-only routes for the Settings tab: list settings, save or clear one (secrets encrypted), and test ntfy, email, YouTube or Cal.com. Writes SiteSettings, reloads SettingsStore, and clears the YouTube video cache when YouTube settings change.

Binds a configuration section to an options class, then overrides its string properties with values saved in the Settings tab through SettingsStore. Registers the change token source so monitors refresh on save. Called from Program.

Holds the Settings tab's saved values in memory, decrypted, and reloads them from the database on save. Encrypts secrets with Data Protection and signals options monitors of changes. Used by SettingsEndpoints and option binding.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Sit.text: Public GET and admin PUT for /site: visitor page and feature visibility, plus maintenance mode. Status is cached in HybridCache, cleared on save, and read from SiteState in PortfolioDbContext. Support, updates and announcements call LoadAsync.
Lists the visitor pages (whatsNew, apps, youtube, about, contact) and the features that can be hidden (coffee, updates, workWithMe). workWithMe stays off until switched on. Used by SiteEndpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Sup.text: Public /support info returning the coffee link when that feature is on. Receives the Buy Me a Coffee webhook, verifies its HMAC signature, stores each donation event once, and sends a phone alert. Admin route lists donations.
The Support configuration section: the Buy me a coffee page URL and the Buy Me a Coffee webhook secret, both editable in the Settings tab. Read by SupportEndpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Ter.text: Two string constants, paragraph and bullets, naming the block types Terms content can contain. Used by TermsDefaults and TermsRules.

Default terms text shown to visitors until the admin first saves their own. It describes what the site records (analytics, contact form, meetings, updates, donations). Changing its date asks visitors to accept again.

Routes under /terms: a public GET that returns the saved terms or the defaults, and an admin-only PUT that validates, normalises and stores new terms with a fresh timestamp. Reads and writes the TermsPages table.

Validates and normalises terms before saving: length limits, required fields, block kinds, and safe links only (http(s) or site paths). Returns errors keyed by JSON path so the editor can show each one beside its input.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Upd.text: When a new app is added and the Apps page and updates are visible, it records a pending announcement and sends the admin a phone alert with Send email and Ignore links. Those links carry a one-time token, checked by its hash.
Constants for an announcement's lifecycle: pending (awaiting the admin), approved, sending, sent, and ignored. The updates emailer moves announcements through these states.

The Email configuration section: Resend API key, sender addresses for general and subscriber mail, and the inbound webhook secret that routes received replies to the Contact inbox. Without a key, emails are only logged.
Development fallback that writes outgoing emails to the log instead of sending them. SwitchingEmailSender uses it when no Resend key is configured.
Sends email through Resend's HTTP API, including attachments, threading headers, and one-click unsubscribe headers. When Resend refuses a send, its reason is passed into the thrown error.
Result values returned when someone subscribes: sent (confirmation on its way), alreadySubscribed, or pending (a confirmation went out recently, so check the inbox).
Chooses the email sender on each send: Resend when an API key is set in configuration or Settings, otherwise the log. It reads options every time, so a newly saved key applies immediately.
The built-in email wording used until an admin saves their own. It covers the confirmation, new-video and new-app emails, plus the footer about why subscribers get them and where replies go.
Constants for the three email kinds: confirm, video and app. The update emails endpoints use them to tell which kind of message is being handled.
Validates and trims the admin's email wording: required fields, length limits, one-line subjects and buttons, safe links, and {title} as the only allowed placeholder. Errors are keyed by field path.

Builds the emails subscribers get, as HTML and plain text, using the admin's wording and the site's styling. Covers the confirmation email and the new video or app emails with unsubscribe links. Also makes a browser-viewable HTML version for previews.

Admin-only API behind the Community tab's email editor. It loads, saves or resets the stored wording, previews an email, and sends a test to the admin's own address. UpdatesAnnouncer and the subscribe flow read the saved wording.

Emails approved new apps and videos to confirmed subscribers, up to 3 items per run, tracking progress as it sends. Skips items hidden from visitors, retries when nothing goes out, and alerts the admin's phone on email failures. Run by UpdatesWorker.

Public API for email updates: subscribe (with double opt-in), confirm and unsubscribe. Admin-only routes list subscribers and announcements and approve or ignore announcements. Approving wakes UpdatesTrigger so emails go out soon.
A signal that wakes UpdatesWorker early, such as when the admin approves an announcement, instead of waiting for its next scheduled run.
Background service that runs UpdatesAnnouncer every 10 minutes, first 30 seconds after startup, and right away when UpdatesTrigger is poked. It logs errors and keeps running.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.Wor.text: Public GET for the hourly Work with me price, which falls back to a default until the admin saves one. An admin-only PUT changes the price after validating currency and amount, and the value is stored in the database.

Holds the allowed currencies for the work-with-me price (EUR, RON, GBP and EU country currencies), the €25/hour default, and a max amount of 100,000. Validates admin-saved prices by currency, amount, and two-decimal precision. Used by WorkWithMeEndpoints.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Features.You.text: Fetches a channel's public uploads from the YouTube Data API v3: resolves the uploads playlist, pages through up to 1,000 videos, and picks the largest thumbnail. Called by YouTubeVideoStore through IYouTubeClient.

Exposes the YouTube channel link and paged video list publicly, plus an admin-only refresh endpoint. Responses are cache-controlled, and the list is served from YouTubeVideoStore, returning 503 when YouTube is unconfigured or unreachable.

The YouTube configuration section, holding the channel (handle or ID) and API key. Reports whether both are set and builds the public channel URL when the channel value is a valid handle or channel ID. Read by several services.

Background service that refreshes the YouTube video store at startup and then hourly, retrying every five minutes after a failure. Skips work when YouTube isn't configured, so visitors rarely wait on YouTube.

Singleton cache of the channel's videos, kept in memory and persisted to the YouTubeSnapshots table so restarts and outages still have a list. Fetches from YouTubeClient on demand and on refresh, and records the last error. Used by YouTube endpoints, the refresh worker, updates, and settings.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.KeyRingDecry.text: Decrypts Data Protection key elements that were sealed by KeyRingEncryptor, using the key from DataProtection:KeyEncryptionKey. Data Protection instantiates it by name with the app's services. Fails with a clear error if that setting is missing.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.KeyRingEncry.text: Provides AES-256-GCM sealing and opening for Data Protection keys, plus parsing of the DataProtection:KeyEncryptionKey setting (32 bytes base64, forgiving of common paste issues). Keys are stored in plain form when the setting is absent, as in local development.
Encrypts the secret part of each Data Protection key before it's written to the database, using KeyRingEncryption.Seal with the configured key. Tags the output so KeyRingDecryptor can read it back.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.Program.text: The application entry point; it creates the WebApplication builder and wires up all feature endpoints, services, and middleware. Configuration comes from appsettings files and the dev launcher script.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.ProxyHeaders.text: Middleware that accepts requests only when the Cloudflare Pages proxy sends the shared secret, otherwise answering 404. It then restores the browser's host, client IP, and country so the rest of the API sees the real visitor. The health check path bypasses it.

backend:class:Portfolio.Api.RequestBodie.text: Helper that reads an incoming request body up to a byte limit, returning null if it's too large. It guards webhook endpoints against oversized bodies whether sent with a declared length or in chunks. Used by contact, meetings, and support.

database:table:public.about_page.text: Stores the About Me page as a single JSON document, read and saved whole, with only one row ever present. Its shape is expected to change often. Used by the About feature and shared code.

database:table:public.admin_sessions.text: Holds one row per signed-in admin device, keyed by a hash of its random cookie token rather than the token itself. Rows are deleted on sign-out or expiry. Used by the auth feature.

database:table:public.alert_channels.text: Records whether each alert channel (ntfy, site notifications) is enabled, toggled in the Notifications tab. A channel with no row counts as enabled. Used by the alerts feature and web push.

database:table:public.alert_preferences.text: Records whether each kind of phone alert is enabled, toggled in the Notifications tab. A kind with no row counts as enabled. Used by the alerts feature and phone alert history.

database:table:public.announcements.text: Queues subscriber emails about new apps or videos; new apps wait for admin approval while videos go out immediately. A unique constraint on kind and key prevents duplicate announcements. Used by updates and settings code.

database:table:public.app_categories.text: Stores the admin-defined kinds of app, such as 'Video game'. Linked to apps and platforms. Used by the Apps feature.

database:table:public.apps.text: Stores each app listed on the Apps page. Linked to categories and platforms and ordered by a shared ordering. Used by the Apps feature.

database:table:public.contact_messages.text: Stores the start of each conversation, from the public contact form or an unknown sender's email to the site address. Admin replies go out by email from that address, and follow-ups are stored as contact replies. Used by the contact feature.

database:table:public.contact_replies.text: Follow-up messages in a contact conversation after the first: the admin's emailed answers and the visitor's emailed replies. Each row links to a contact_messages row. Used by the contact feature and shared email, conversation, and meeting code.

database:table:public.data_protection_ke.text: ASP.NET Core Data Protection key ring, stored in the database so encryption keys survive restarts. Used by the shared data-protection setup that encrypts saved secrets.

database:table:public.donations.text: Payments reported by Buy Me a Coffee's webhook, including donations, memberships, and extras. Used by the support feature and shared tests, settings, and support/resume code.

database:table:public.leetcode_stats.text: The last LeetCode stats fetched for each user, kept so they survive restarts and can still display when LeetCode is unreachable. Used by the leetcode feature and shared LeetCode stats code.

database:table:public.meetings.text: Meetings booked through Cal.com from the Contact page, stored as the webhook reported them. The admin accepts or declines requests here or from the phone alert. Used by the meetings feature and shared meeting and reply code.

database:table:public.phone_alerts.text: History of phone alerts the site raised, whether sent, skipped (kind switched off or no destination set), or failed. Backs the Notifications tab. Written by the alerts feature, read by shared alert history and web push code.

database:table:public.profiles.text: The site owner's profile data. Used by the profile feature and shared admin session and initial-setup code.

database:table:public.push_devices.text: Browsers subscribed to the site's Web Push notifications, such as the admin's iPhone home-screen app or a desktop browser. Stores each push service address and its encryption keys. Used by alerts and shared web push code.

database:table:public.resume.text: Single-row résumé settings from the About Me page: the admin's choices, private contact details, and the last two generated PDFs. Private contact details never reach the public About Me JSON. Used by resume and shared settings and support code.

database:table:public.site_settings.text: Connection settings saved in the Settings tab, such as the Resend API key, which override matching configuration values. Secrets are stored encrypted and never returned to the browser. Used by the settings feature and shared settings code.

database:table:public.site_state.text: Single row holding which pages and setup-dependent features visitors can see, plus the maintenance flag. Edited from the Settings tab and read by the site-state code.

database:table:public.stored_files.text: Stores files the admin uploads, such as the About Me photo and résumé, in the database. Accessed through IFileStorage, so it could later move to object storage.

database:table:public.subscribers.text: Email addresses of people who asked for new-post notifications. They receive updates only after confirming (double opt-in), and unsubscribing deletes the row. Also touched by shared support and resume code.

database:table:public.terms_page.text: Holds the terms and conditions as one JSON document, read and saved as a whole. There is always exactly one row. Content structure is defined in TermsContent.cs.

database:table:public.update_emails.text: Holds the wording of subscriber update emails as one JSON document, always one row. Built-in defaults apply until the admin saves custom wording from the updates email page.

database:table:public.updates_state.text: Single row recording when announcements began. Only apps and videos posted after that point are announced, so early subscribers don't receive the existing backlog.

database:table:public.visit_events.text: Logs events during a visit, such as page opens, clicks, and errors. Each event belongs to a visit_sessions row. Recording rules are in AnalyticsRules.cs.

database:table:public.visit_sessions.text: One row per browser tab visit. The id comes from sessionStorage, so a page reload counts as the same visit. The signed-in admin's visits are never recorded.

database:table:public.web_push_keys.text: Stores the site's VAPID P-256 key pair for Web Push. It's generated once on first use and kept permanently, since replacing it would break every device that allowed notifications.

database:table:public.work_with_me_price.text: Single row holding the hourly price for Work with me, as set by the admin. The default price applies until the admin first saves one.

database:table:public.youtube_videos.text: Stores the last list of videos fetched for a YouTube channel, so it survives restarts and can be shown when YouTube is unreachable. Read and written through YouTubeSnapshot in the youtube feature, and used by YouTubeVideos in shared.

feature:about@backend.text: Serves and saves the About Me page (GET/PUT /api/about) as one JSON document: AboutJson reads it (upgrading older shapes), AboutRules validates and normalises it with errors keyed by JSON path, and AboutDefaults stands in until the admin first saves. The other classes are the fixed vocabularies the page uses: language levels, licence categories, NeetCode lists, skill uses and kinds of place visit.

feature:about@database.text: about_page: a single row holding the whole About Me page as JSON, with when it was last saved.

feature:about@frontend.text: The public About page and its admin editor, covering profile, statuses, skills chart, timeline, qualifications, hackathons, languages, licences, papers, a world map of places, and LeetCode and NeetCode stats. Visitors see read-only sections; the admin edits in place and each section saves on demand. The page loads and saves as one whole document through the about API, which also serves LeetCode stats and the admin-only résumé contact fields. Photo and paper uploads go through the files API, and collapsed-section state is kept in browser localStorage.

feature:admin@frontend.text: The admin's sign-in page (/admin): a Sign in with Google button that goes through the API, a skeleton while the session is checked, and why the last attempt failed.

feature:alerts@backend.text: Phone alerts for the admin: PhoneAlerts queues them, AlertWorker sends them through ntfy and Web Push unless their kind or channel is switched off (AlertPreferences, kept in memory), and every alert is logged. CrashAlertHandler raises one for an unhandled API error (at most hourly per kind). The Notifications endpoints switch kinds and channels on or off, list the history and register push devices, with the site's own VAPID keys.

feature:alerts@database.text: Alert switches (alert_preferences per kind, alert_channels per channel), the log of every alert raised (phone_alerts), the browsers registered for Web Push (push_devices) and the site's VAPID key pair (web_push_keys).

feature:alerts@frontend.text: One view model: every kind of phone alert, grouped as the API orders them, each with an on/off switch (used by the Notifications tab).

feature:analytics@backend.text: First-party visitor analytics, no cookies or third parties: the browser's tracker posts events, AnalyticsRules decides what may be recorded and tidies it, VisitorHasher turns IP and User-Agent into a daily visitor id, and AnalyticsRetention deletes visits past the retention the terms promise. The admin reads summaries, lists visits and replays or deletes one.

feature:analytics@database.text: visit_sessions (one per browser tab visit: device, browser, country, entry page, counts) and visit_events (each page view, click or error in it, in order).

feature:analytics@frontend.text: Records anonymous visitors' page views, clicks, errors and theme switches, but only after they accept the terms, and never for the admin. Events are sent in batches to the analytics API. The admin's Engagement dashboard reads period summaries, paged visit lists and visit details from that API, showing stat tiles, a traffic chart, ranked lists and replayable visit timelines. The admin can also delete visits.

feature:apps@backend.text: The Apps page's data: list, create, edit, reorder and delete apps and their categories, plus what What's new? shows. AppRules validates an app (errors keyed by JSON path, YouTube links recognised as in the frontend); deleting an app also clears its pending update announcement and unused uploads.

feature:apps@database.text: apps (title, description, categories, platforms, links, media) and app_categories (the kinds the admin defined, in order).

feature:apps@frontend.text: The public Apps grid and app detail popups, plus admin tools to create, edit and delete apps, manage categories, reorder apps and choose the What's new app. Reads and writes go through the apps API, with YouTube data pulled from the same API. Media uploads go through the files API. Visitors see nine apps per page; the admin sees eight plus an Add tile. The whole display order is saved at once.

feature:auth@backend.text: Google sign-in for the single admin: GoogleSignIn accepts only allowed, verified accounts; AdminSessionService keeps one session per device, the cookie carrying a random token whose hash is stored. Endpoints report who is signed in, list the signed-in devices and sign one or all others out; SameOriginWrites adds a second guard against cross-site writes.

feature:auth@database.text: admin_sessions: one row per signed-in device (hashed token, email, browser, country, when it started and expires).

feature:auth@frontend.text: Admin sign-in, session handling and navigation. The app checks the session on load, extends it on activity, and syncs sign-in and sign-out across browser tabs. The Settings page lists the admin's signed-in devices and can end one or all others. Sign-out affects only the current device. Auth state lives in Redux and is read through the auth API. Visitors see only enabled navigation tabs.

feature:contact@backend.text: Conversations with visitors: the public contact form posts a message (ContactRules, mirrored by the frontend), emails to the site's address arrive through Resend's inbound webhook and join their conversation, and the admin lists, reads, replies to (by email) and deletes them. Meetings also read and write these messages, which the rules flag as a cross-feature write.

feature:contact@database.text: contact_messages (the first message of each conversation, from the form or an email) and contact_replies (every message after it, either way).

feature:contact@frontend.text: The public contact form and the admin's message inbox. Visitors' messages are sent through the contact API, and Send stays disabled until every field is valid. The admin sees a paged inbox of 10 messages per page, with the page number kept in the URL, and it refreshes every minute. From there the admin can open, delete or reply to messages, and replies are emailed to the sender. Meetings booked by a sender appear alongside their message.

feature:featuretesting@frontend.text: The admin-only Feature Testing tab (BETA): new features tried out on the real site before visitors get them, one page per feature with its own navigation.

feature:files@backend.text: Uploads by the admin (the About Me photo, papers, app media) stored as database rows: FileRules checks the type and prepares photos, the endpoints upload and serve them, and FileCleanup deletes files nothing references any more (it reads apps to know, a cross-feature read the rules flag).

feature:files@database.text: stored_files: the uploaded files themselves (bytes, type, name, when).

feature:files@frontend.text: Admin-only upload calls for three kinds of file: photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF up to 15 MB), academic papers (PDF up to 200 MB), and app media (images or MP4, MOV or WebM video). The About and Apps editors use these calls. Uploads happen immediately, but the page only uses an uploaded file after its section is saved.

feature:leetcode@backend.text: LeetCode stats for About Me without hitting LeetCode on every view: LeetCodeClient reads the public GraphQL profile data, cached in memory and as a database snapshot that survives restarts and is shown when LeetCode is down.

feature:leetcode@database.text: leetcode_stats: the last stats fetched per username, as JSON, with when.

feature:leetcode@frontend.text: Public call that fetches LeetCode stats for the username set on the About Me page, returning null when none is set. Its single part, leetcodeEndpoints, is used by aboutApi and reports 404 for an unknown user or 503 when the service is unreachable. It reads external LeetCode data and writes nothing.

feature:meetings@backend.text: Meetings by invitation through Cal.com: the admin sends the booking link in a reply, Cal.com's webhook reports bookings, and the admin accepts, declines or cancels with an optional emailed note (PersonalEmails). MeetingReminders sends phone reminders a day, two hours and five minutes before, and at the start.

feature:meetings@database.text: meetings: each booking as Cal.com reported it (attendee, times, status, the decision token's hash).

feature:meetings@frontend.text: Admin's Cal.com meetings on the Contact page: a month calendar with status dots, the selected day's meetings, and a pending-request count. Accept, decline, or cancel actions go through meetingsApi, which updates Cal.com and emails attendees. The feature also bundles a WebGL 'Riviera' background with a still-image fallback, and reportSlowScene switches visitors who haven't picked a theme to their system light or dark theme when the Vice scene draws slowly, saved in localStorage.

feature:notifications@frontend.text: Admin-only Notifications page for choosing which alerts reach the admin and where: ntfy and site notifications, per-kind phone switches, and push devices. AlertChannelsCard and Here handle channel toggles and this browser's push status, Kinds shows each kind's 30-day count and last-sent time, and History lists sent or held notifications with filtering and pagination. Their view models call notificationsApi, which saves toggles optimistically and manages push devices via notificationsEndpoints. Non-admins who open the page are sent home.

feature:places@backend.text: City search for About Me's places: CityIndex loads every place with 1,000+ people from GeoNames into memory and searches them by name.

feature:places@frontend.text: Admin city search that returns cities matching a typed name, largest first, optionally narrowed by region or country. Its single part, placesEndpoints, is used by aboutApi. It reads city data and writes nothing.

feature:preview@frontend.text: The admin's preview switch (in development): see the site normally, while loading, or when loading fails, by holding or failing GET requests; and the admin bar it sits in.

feature:profile@backend.text: The first-name endpoint (GET /api/firstname), from the original template: one Profile row.

feature:profile@frontend.text: Public call that returns the site owner's first name from /api/firstname. Its single part, profileEndpoints, has no callers listed in the map, so it may be unused or wired in elsewhere. It only reads the first name and writes nothing.

feature:resume@backend.text: A résumé generated from the About Me page: the admin picks sections, skills and the private header (email, phone, headline), and generating lays it out with QuestPDF as two PDFs, a public one and a private one with contact details, stored until the next run.

feature:resume@database.text: resume: the admin's choices, private contact details and the two generated PDFs.

feature:resume@frontend.text: Lets the admin on the About Me page choose résumé sections and hidden skills, save them, and generate public and private PDFs; the private copy includes email and phone. ResumePanel and its view model drive this, with ResumeDownloads showing generation time and download links and ResumeSkeleton as a loading placeholder. resumeApi saves settings, generates PDFs, and fetches the public headline, invalidating the About cache after generating; whenFulfilled helps endpoints update state after saves.

feature:settings@backend.text: The Settings tab's connections: keys and links for every outside service, grouped by SettingsCatalog, encrypted at rest and kept in memory by SettingsStore, which overrides the configuration and tells options to reload. Each service can be tested from the tab.

feature:settings@database.text: site_settings: each saved setting (key, value, whether it's encrypted, when).

feature:settings@frontend.text: Admin-only Settings page for connections to outside services (Buy Me a Coffee, Cal.com, Google sign-in, hosting, ntfy), each as an expandable card. Saved values are stored encrypted through the settings API and override server configuration; stored values can be removed, and secrets are never displayed. Test buttons run connection checks, and a generator creates a random private ntfy topic name. Reads and writes app settings via settingsApi and settingsEndpoints.

feature:shared@backend.text: What every feature stands on: Program (the composition root), PortfolioDbContext, proxy-header handling behind Cloudflare, the Redis key prefix, webhook body limits, and encryption of the Data Protection key ring.

feature:shared@database.text: data_protection_keys: the encrypted keys that protect the sign-in cookie and the saved secrets.

feature:shared@frontend.text: Library of reusable UI building blocks used across the app: modal dialogs, copy and delete buttons, pagination, a paged grid, an on/off switch, empty and error states, skeleton loaders, icon wrappers, and date formatting. Also holds the base API plumbing (baseApi, run, post, toLoadable, usePagedQuery) that feature endpoints build on. AdminOnly gates admin pages using the auth status from Redux. Stores no data of its own, though PagedGrid keeps its page number in the URL.

feature:site@backend.text: What visitors can see: one SiteState row with each page and feature switched on or off, and maintenance mode with a message (GET/PUT /api/site).

feature:site@database.text: site_state: visible pages and features, and maintenance on/off with its message.

feature:site@frontend.text: Controls site-wide visibility. It decides whether visitors see the site, the maintenance screen, or the unreachable screen, and which pages, features, and tabs are shown. Admins toggle pages, features, and maintenance mode, with an optional message, in Settings; changes save immediately through siteEndpoints. Public site status loads on startup and retries while the API is down. Also handles app layout state, swipe navigation, scroll memory, and the idle watcher.

feature:support@backend.text: Buy Me a Coffee: the header button's link (configurable in Settings), and the webhook that records each donation or membership for the Community tab.

feature:support@database.text: donations: each payment Buy Me a Coffee reported (amount, currency, who, test or not).

feature:support@frontend.text: Buy Me a Coffee support on the site. A header 'Buy me a coffee' button links to the donation page URL from the API's Support:Url setting, and is hidden when the feature is off or no link is set. Admins see a paged Donations table on the Community page showing sender, amount, message, and received time, with test donations tagged. Data comes from communityApi and supportEndpoints; button clicks are tracked as analytics events.

feature:terms@backend.text: The terms and conditions as one JSON document (GET/PUT /api/terms): TermsRules validates, TermsDefaults is the starting text, block kinds define paragraphs and lists.

feature:terms@database.text: terms_page: a single row holding the whole terms document as JSON.

feature:terms@frontend.text: Terms and conditions for the site. Visitors must tick each consent and accept the current version through a non-dismissable welcome gate; the admin is exempt. Acceptance is remembered per browser in localStorage, and the terms can be read in a popup or on the Terms page. Admins edit sections and paragraphs, and each save forces visitors to accept again. Also holds the theme system: saved theme choice in localStorage, the dark/light/Vice switch, and automatic fallback on low-power devices. Data via termsApi and termsEndpoints.

feature:updates@backend.text: Email updates: visitors subscribe with double opt-in, and UpdatesAnnouncer (run by UpdatesWorker, or at once via UpdatesTrigger) emails confirmed subscribers about new apps and videos; new apps wait for the admin's send-or-ignore decision. The admin edits the emails' wording with a preview and a test send; sending goes through Resend, or the log in development.

feature:updates@database.text: subscribers, announcements (what to email, its decision and recipients), update_emails (the wording as JSON) and updates_state (from when announcing started).

feature:updates@frontend.text: Email updates signup and management. Visitors subscribe through a double opt-in dialog, and confirmation and unsubscribe links are handled on landing pages. Admins view subscribers, send or ignore pending announcements, and edit the three update email templates with a live preview and a test send. Data flows through communityApi and updatesEndpoints, with subscriber records and announcement status stored server-side.

feature:whatsnew@frontend.text: What's new: the newest app or YouTube video, whichever came last among the sections visitors may see, shown in full in one card.

feature:workwithme@backend.text: Work with me's hourly price: anyone reads it, the admin sets the amount and currency (WorkWithMePrices lists the allowed currencies); €25 until first saved.

feature:workwithme@database.text: work_with_me_price: one row with the amount, currency and when it was set.

feature:workwithme@frontend.text: Work With Me is the services section of the frontend: offered services, project steps, and the hourly price at the bottom. Visitors see the rate read-only, while a signed-in admin gets an edit form for its currency and amount, using a currency picker with EUR, RON and GBP listed first. Prices are read and saved through the workWithMe API, which defaults to €25 until set. Typed amounts are checked by parseAmount and shown with formatPrice.

feature:youtube@backend.text: The channel's videos via the YouTube Data API: YouTubeVideoStore keeps them in memory and as a database snapshot, YouTubeRefreshWorker refreshes them on start and periodically, and the admin can refresh on demand (errors kept for the refresh popup).

feature:youtube@database.text: youtube_videos: the last list fetched per channel, as JSON.

feature:youtube@frontend.text: YouTube shows the author's channel videos newest first, nine per page, in a grid. Tiles open on YouTube, and the detail view embeds the player with the full description. Admins get a refresh button that fetches new videos now instead of waiting for the hourly refresh, with a copyable error report on failure. Data comes from the youtube and apps APIs, and the grid and What's New reload after a refresh.

frontend-viewmodels:symbol:frontend/src/.text: Decides whether a visitor sees the site, the maintenance screen, or an unreachable-API screen. Signed-in users and the sign-in, confirm, and unsubscribe routes always get through. Also starts the session keeper, loads site settings, and sets the admin app manifest. Used by App.
Returns the signed-in user from Redux auth state, or null when signed out or while the session is loading. Used by the SignedIn component in the auth feature.
Returns true only after the session check confirms nobody is signed in, so the SignedOut component does not show during loading. Used by SignedOut in the auth feature.
Exposes the current auth status from Redux so the shared AdminOnly wrapper can decide whether to render its children.
Runs the dialog's async confirm action, shows a failure state if it throws, and closes only on success. Blocks closing while busy. Used by ConfirmDialog in the meetings feature.
Copies a given string to the clipboard and briefly shows copied or failed feedback, including tooltip and screen-reader text. Used by the shared CopyButton component.
Tracks whether the delete confirmation popup is open, with actions to open and close it. Holds no data of its own. Used by the shared DeleteButton component.
Provides a unique element id for the shared ErrorState component.
Works out each option's checked state and toggle handler for a multi-select checkbox group. Toggled values are always returned in the options' original order.
Supplies the ids and change handler for a colour input, passing the chosen colour string to onChange. Includes an error id when an error is shown.
Manages the add-link draft for a text field: it takes the selected text and a URL, validates the URL, and inserts [text](url) at the selection. Enter inserts the link, and Escape closes the draft.
Splits a month and year input into separate controls and emits the value as the first day of the month (YYYY-MM-01). It keeps a partly typed year and resyncs when the value changes from outside.
Supplies ids, ARIA wiring, and the change handler for a text field. It also records the last cursor selection so 'Add link' knows where to insert.
Provides a page-unique id for the cup's inside, which the coffee fill is drawn into. This keeps multiple coffee icons on one page from clashing.
Returns a page-unique id for the icon's gradient, so several Instagram icons can share a page without clashing.

Handles modal behavior: moves focus in on open and back to the opener on close, keeps Tab inside the dialog, and locks page scroll. Escape and backdrop clicks close it unless it is not dismissible. Used by the shared Modal component.
Holds the current page in the URL, its items from the store, and page navigation that scrolls to the top. It prefetches neighbouring pages and slides pages in and out unless reduced motion is on.
Handles one file upload for the About section. It rejects files over the size limit, uploads the rest with a progress percentage, and builds the button and error labels.
Edits one hackathon's name, year, and bullets in the About section. The year text is kept while typing and written back only once it is a valid year, and it also supplies field errors.
Editor logic for the hackathons list in the About section. It sorts by year, adds a blank entry at the top, and edits, moves or removes rows. Changes go up through onChange and persist only on Save.
Turns hackathons into timeline items for the read-only About view. Each shows the name as the title, the year as the period, and the bullet points as details. Used by the HackathonsSection component.

Form logic for one language's name and level. It supplies the level options and labels, and builds the legend and field names from the row's position. Edits are passed up through onChange to the LanguageEditor component.

Manages the list of languages in the About editor, one row per language with its name and level errors. It handles edit, move and remove, and adds new languages at the end as beginners. Used by the LanguagesEditor component.
Prepares languages for the read-only About view. Each shows its name, a level label, and a five-step bar with the steps filled to match the level. Used by the LanguagesSection component.

Manages licences in the About editor. It shows catalogue licences as toggles grouped by category, lists the admin's custom licences with their errors, and adds custom ones while ignoring duplicates. Changes go up through onChange.
Pure sorting function for licences. Catalogue licences come first in catalogue order, followed by custom licences in the order they were added. Used by useLicencesSectionViewModel.
Groups licences by category for the read-only About view, sorts each group with inDisplayOrder, and omits categories with no licences. Used by the LicencesSection component.

Holds the draft for a custom licence: category, optional code and name. It requires a name, trims inputs, and passes the result to onAdd before clearing the fields. Enter adds the licence instead of submitting the parent form.

Handles one paper's title and PDF in the About editor. It builds a safe download link and file name, sets the upload size limit, and lets the user upload, replace or remove the file. Used by the PaperEditor component.
Builds the rows for the papers editor: each paper's title and file errors, plus move, remove and add. PDF uploads set the file on the latest list. Used by PapersEditor.
Turns each paper into a download link when it has a safe PDF URL, otherwise plain title text. Used by PapersSection to show the public About papers list.
Searches cities from the store once two or more letters are typed, debounced, largest first, with labels and region details. Picking a city clears the query. Used by CitySearch.
Works out the map pin's shape: one filled disc for a single colour, or equal clockwise slices for several colours, plus outline width. Used by MapPin, with no external calls.
Holds the worked, studied and visited ticks for one place, each with an optional note, and requires at least one tick before applying. Used by PlacePopup.

Manages the places editor: colours per visit kind, the alphabetical place list, the map highlight, and the popup for a picked city or existing place. Changes stay local until the section is saved. Used by PlacesEditor.
Supplies the places legend, with a coloured dot and label per visit kind, a zoom hint, and whether there are no places yet. Used by PlacesSection.
Controls the interactive world map: zoom buttons, Ctrl/Cmd-scroll and pinch zoom, drag to pan, pin hover and pinned cards, and analytics events for map use. Used by WorldMap.
Loads LeetCode stats by username through the about API and derives the card state, including hidden for visitors when the user isn't found and a stale date after two days. Used by LeetCodeCard.
Edits the LeetCode username (a pasted profile link is reduced to the name) and toggles the NeetCode lists. Changes go through the parent's onChange. Used by ProblemSolvingEditor.
Decides whether the problem-solving section has anything to show, and prepares the LeetCode username and NeetCode list labels for display. Used by ProblemSolvingSection.
Computes the arcs of the solved-problems ring, one per difficulty with solved problems, plus a formatted total count. Takes LeetCode solved stats; used by SolvedRing.
Handles edits to the profile draft: photo upload and removal, profile links, status list, and the admin's résumé contact fields. Used by ProfileEditor; uses the shared ResumeContact type.

Prepares the public profile view: safe, non-empty links, the photo, headline, and statuses. For admins it also exposes private email and phone, with a retry path if loading fails. Used by ProfileSection.
Manages one status label's text and flag. The flag is auto-guessed from the text until the user picks one manually; unknown saved flags remain selectable. Used by StatusEditor.
Turns the status list into editable rows, each with its own error, change, move and remove handlers, and provides adding a new empty status. Used by StatusesEditor.
Handles the fields of a single qualification (title, issuer, obtained date, grade) and produces its numbered labels. Used by QualificationEditor.
Turns the qualifications list into editable rows with per-field errors, reorder and remove handlers, and an add action that defaults the date to the current month. Used by QualificationsEditor.
Converts saved qualifications into display-ready items, with the obtained date formatted as month text and a machine-readable datetime, and grade shown as 'Grade: X'. Used by QualificationsSection.
Turns a list of bullet texts into editable rows that can be edited, reordered, or removed, plus an add action. Labels are derived from the item name. Used by BulletsEditor.

Remembers whether each About section is collapsed, saved in browser localStorage under the section title. If storage is unavailable, such as in private mode, collapsing still works but isn't remembered. Used by useEditableSectionViewModel.

Drives an About section card: collapse toggle for all visitors, and for the admin an edit draft with save, cancel, and save error messages. Uses useCollapsed and describeSaveError; used by the EditableSection component.
Handles one skill period's fields: start, end, the still-using-it toggle, and which uses apply, with per-field errors. Ticking still-using clears the end date. Used by the PeriodEditor component.

Manages one skill in the admin editor: its name, its periods (add, change, remove), and a summary of time used. The skill stays expanded while it has validation errors. Used by the SkillEditor component.

Builds the About skills chart: a legend of the uses that appear, one row per skill with positioned bars, year ticks, and a marker for now. Relies on date and layout helpers. Used by the SkillsChart component.
Manages the admin skills list: which skills are expanded (tracked by position), add, move, remove, sort by experience, and the colour for each use. Used by the SkillsEditor component.

Manages the admin list of timeline entries: order, add (new entry on top), move, remove, and sort by end date with ongoing first. Save persists the order, and Cancel undoes it. Used by the TimelineEditor component.
Edits one timeline entry's fields (title, organization, location, dates, ongoing toggle, bullets) and maps API error keys to each field and bullet. Used by the TimelineEntryEditor component.
Converts stored timeline items into the view shape the public About timeline displays. Used by the TimelineSection component.

Feeds page views, theme switches, and terms acceptance to the analytics tracker. Nothing is recorded until the visitor accepts the terms, and admin sessions are never recorded. Uses Tracker and useTerms; used by the AnalyticsTracker component.
Builds the analytics bar chart at the container's measured width. Handles metric switching, axis ticks, bar geometry, axis and hover labels, and the tooltip, using the series data and bucket size.
Tracks an element's width in CSS pixels with ResizeObserver, defaulting to 640 when ResizeObserver is unavailable. The series chart uses it to size itself to its container.
Loads one analytics visit by id through the analytics API. Exposes its loading state, a title showing when the visit started, and a retry action for the VisitDialog component.

Manages the paged analytics visits table: current page (kept in local state, not the URL), the errors-only filter, the open visit, and deleting a visit. Deleting refreshes the list through cache tags.

Handles viewing, editing and creating an app in the apps dialog. Manages the draft, asks before discarding unsaved changes, saves and deletes through the apps API, and maps server field errors to form fields.
Prepares an app tile for display: picks its image (first image or YouTube thumbnail), strips link markup from the description, and calls onOpen when the tile is opened.
Provides the app category list, read from the same cached query the Apps page uses for admins, plus an editing flag with start and stop actions for the CategoriesButton.
Edits the app category list as one draft (rename, reorder, add, remove) and saves it together through the apps API. Shows per-row errors and asks before discarding unsaved changes.
Turns the available app categories into toggle options. When one is toggled, the selected IDs are returned in the categories' order, and an empty flag shows when no categories exist.
Maps an app's links to editable rows with label and URL fields, their validation errors, and add and remove actions. Supplies the store-name suggestions used by the apps form.

Tracks which slide an app's media carousel shows, whether it moved by swipe, scroll, arrows, dots or arrow keys. It pauses videos when they leave view and sends slide-change analytics events. Used by the MediaCarousel component.

Manages an app's media list in the editor: drag-to-reorder, uploading several files with progress and per-file size checks, and adding media from a link. Uploads call the files API, and the list is saved with the app.
Decides what one carousel slide displays: an image, a video, a YouTube player when active or its thumbnail otherwise, or nothing if the YouTube link is invalid. Used by the MediaSlide component.
Chooses the preview for a media item: images as themselves, YouTube videos as their thumbnail, and other videos as their own source for a first-frame preview. Used by the MediaThumbnail component.
Holds the open or closed state of the app organise dialog and exposes open and close actions. Used by the OrganiseButton component.

Lets the admin reorder apps in a draft and save the whole order at once, with unsaved-change warnings and a per-app 'show in What's New' toggle. Loads and saves the app order and handles conflicts when apps changed meanwhile. Used by the OrganiseDialog component.
Supplies a unique label id so the platform list is announced as 'Runs on' for screen readers. A small accessibility helper with no data of its own. Used by the PlatformChips component.
Shows common platforms plus any custom ones as toggles, and adds a custom platform from a text box, ignoring case duplicates. Pressing Enter adds it. Used by the PlatformsEditor component.
Filters an app's store links down to safe URLs and turns each into a 'Check it on' label for display. Used by the StoreLinks component.

Backs the Settings page listing the admin's signed-in devices. It loads sessions, signs out one device or all others, and shows loading, success and error messages. Uses the sessions API and the shared date and error helpers.

Holds the contact form's values, errors, and send state. Blocks Send until fields are valid, reports invalid fields to analytics, and submits via the contact API. Topic is fixed or chosen when the Work with me feature is on.
Loads one contact message, polling every minute so emailed answers appear. Marks it read once loaded and still unread, and exposes a retry for failed loads.

Manages the reply draft for a contact message and sends it through the contact API, which emails it to the sender with their message quoted. Can insert the booking link from meetings, and shows errors for failed sends.

Drives the contact inbox: a paged message list stored in the ?page= URL parameter, auto-refreshing every minute, plus the open message and delete. Clicking a row opens it, except when a button inside it is clicked.

Handles accepting or declining a meeting request with an optional message, and cancelling an accepted meeting with an optional reason. Calls the meetings API, which reports to Cal.com and emails attendees, and shows errors for failed actions.

Builds the month calendar view of meetings fetched from the meetings API for the visible month. Groups meetings by day, tracks the selected day, counts pending requests, and provides month navigation.

Manages alert channels (each toggled on or off) and browser push devices via the notifications API. Works out whether this browser is subscribed, lets the user allow or stop it, and sends test notifications or removes devices.
Reads the current preview mode from the Redux preview slice and exposes the mode options with their checked state. Choosing an option dispatches a mode change to the store.

Loads saved résumé settings and keeps an editable draft of sections and hidden skills. Saves the draft or generates both résumés through the resume API, then exposes private and public download URLs with a version tag.
Supplies the title, text, and retry action for the maintenance or unreachable screen. Retry dispatches the site fetch from the site feature, which reloads the site state.

Drives the site visibility settings screen. It loads site state, toggles page, feature, and maintenance switches through saveSite, and edits the maintenance message. It shows a note when the coffee feature is on but has no support link.
Supplies a unique id for an on/off switch. Used by the Switch component in the site feature.
For a given site page, reports whether to show it (null while loading). If the page is hidden, it gives the path of the first visible tab, or /coming-soon when none is visible.
Supplies the support button's link from the support query. It hides the button when the coffee feature is off or the request fails, and tracks clicks as analytics events.
Controls the terms popup. It exposes the loaded terms state, a title, and reload and close actions, and closes the popup when the user navigates to another page.
Formats the 'Last updated' line for a terms document. It returns null if the terms have never been saved.
Backs the terms acceptance gate, which cannot be dismissed. It tracks each consent checkbox, reports when all are ticked, and dispatches acceptance of the current terms version.
Loads the terms and reports whether the user must accept them. It also reports whether the welcome popup and the terms popup are open.
Holds the open and closed state of the subscribe dialog, with show and close actions.
Handles email signup. It validates the address, calls subscribe, tracks the outcome, and maps errors to messages. It also shows the confirmation text for the double opt-in email.
Returns a value only after it has stopped changing for a set delay, or immediately on first use. Used by useUpdateEmailsEditorViewModel to delay the email preview while the admin types.

Manages the admin's editing of the three update-email wordings (confirm, video, app): loads them, shows a live preview, saves or resets to defaults, and sends a test email. Used by UpdateEmailsEditor.
Builds the 'New app' card's label, formatted creation date, and title from an app's details. Used by the LatestApp component in What's new.
Builds the 'New video' card's label, formatted publish date, and title from a YouTube video. Used by the LatestVideo component in What's new.

Handles mouse and keyboard behaviour for a select-only currency dropdown following the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern. Takes the current code and an onChange callback. Used by the CurrencyPicker component.
Checks typed price text (accepts a dot or comma, up to two decimals, within a maximum) and returns either the amount or a user-facing error. Used by useWorkWithMePriceViewModel.
Provides the hourly Work With Me price for display, and for signed-in admins an edit state to change its currency and amount, saved through the workWithMe API. Used by WorkWithMePrice.
Turns a failed YouTube refresh's status into a plain sentence: unreachable API, expired session, YouTube unavailable or not set up, or a generic error. Used by useRefreshVideosButtonViewModel.
Builds a plain-text, line-by-line report of a failed YouTube refresh (time, request, status, API detail, cause) for the user to copy. Used by useRefreshVideosButtonViewModel.

Triggers the YouTube refresh mutation and tracks its idle, busy, done, or failed phase, with a screen-reader announcement and error details. The video grid and What's new reload afterwards. Used by RefreshVideosButton.
Builds the embed URL for the YouTube player from a video's ID. Used by the VideoDetailsView component in the youtube feature, using the shared youTubeEmbedUrl helper.
Formats a video's publish date for display and also returns the raw ISO timestamp for the machine-readable datetime attribute. Used by the VideoTile component in the youtube feature.

Gives the YouTube channel button its link: the channel page, or the page with the subscribe prompt when requested. Fetches the channel URL through the apps API and returns null until it loads or if no channel is set.

Supplies the admin bar's state for a signed-in admin: their email, whether maintenance mode is on, the dev-only preview switch, and sign-out. Uses the auth hook and reads site maintenance status from the Redux store.

Provides state for the main app layout: the admin's preview mode, the Vice theme and its hide-content toggle, the updates feature flag, scroll memory, and swipe navigation between pages. Pulls from the site slice and the theme state in the store.

Runs the scene on the background canvas, falling back to a still image when WebGL 2 is missing, the scene fails, it runs too slowly, or reduced motion is set. Restarts it if the browser restores a lost WebGL context.

Controls the Hide/Show page button, including its label, placement in the header or bottom-right corner on narrow screens, and idle fade. While the page is hidden, it adds classes to the document root and handles Escape to restore the page.

Tracks the current page and the one sliding out during navigation, choosing the slide direction from tab order or a swipe. Skips animation when motion is not allowed and clears the leaving page after 800ms as a fallback.

Supplies the site footer with the current year and a function to open the terms. The footer is hidden while the welcome popup is open, since the popup has its own terms link. Uses the terms feature hook.

Shows a notice when Vice ran too slowly and the site switched to another theme, and auto-dismisses it after a delay. Lets the visitor keep Vice, which records it as their choice, or dismiss the notice. Reads the theme state from the store.
Builds the System navigation links, shown only to a signed-in admin on a System page and hidden for visitors. Uses the auth hook and the current router location to mark the active page.

Builds the navigation tabs: visitors see only enabled pages, while the admin sees all of them with hidden ones marked. Also drives the sliding highlight under the current tab, mouse dragging of that highlight, and scroll arrows on narrow screens.

Supplies the theme picker's options and current selection from the Redux theme state, and dispatches a change when one is chosen. Marks the just-picked option so its icon animates, but not on load or on automatic theme changes.
Shows developer-only visitor test tools, only under npm run dev while nobody is signed in. Its reset action clears the remembered terms acceptance so the welcome popup returns, then reloads the page.
