Loads the About page and saves edits by sending the whole page with one section changed. For the admin, also loads and saves private résumé contact details. Gives each section its value and save handler, plus the public headline and YouTube link.
Drives the admin sign-in page: shows a loading state, sends an already-signed-in admin home, turns a failed Google sign-in error into a readable message, and provides the Google sign-in link.
Controls the Apps page. The admin gets category data and an Add tile, with 8 apps per page; visitors get 9 per page. Tracks which app's detail popup is open, including when a new app is being added.

Backs the announcements list on the Community page: pages through announcements and lets the admin send or ignore each one, showing an error if that fails. Keeps polling while any email is sending so its status updates without a reload.
Provides the donations list for the Support page, one page at a time, by wrapping the shared paged-list hook around the donations query.
Adds page-number state to any paginated query, kept in memory rather than the URL since one tab can hold several lists. Used by the announcements, donations and subscribers view models.
Lists subscribers one page at a time and can delete one by id. Calls the community API for both; used by the Subscribers view on the Community page.

Turns the confirmation link's result into the message shown: working, subscribed (with email if known), test email, invalid link, or failure. Shows the YouTube section only when subscribed. Used by ConfirmSubscriptionPage.
Reports whether the auth state is still loading, so the Contact page can show the form's shape until it knows who the visitor is. Reads the auth slice from the store; used by ContactPage.

Holds the selected analytics period (default 30 days), its summary with country codes turned into names, and refresh and retry actions. Refresh invalidates the Summary, Visits and Visit caches. Calls the analytics API; used by Dashboard.

Picks the open feature from the URL slug, defaulting to the first, and builds navigation links for the list. Redirects to the first feature when no slug is given, or back to /features when the slug is unknown. Used by FeatureTesting.

Pages through raised notifications, newest first, optionally filtered by kind, with labels for each kind. Builds the 'sent to' text, links only same-site paths, and refresh reloads history and kind counts. Calls the notifications API; used by History.
Loads phone alert kinds, groups them in API order, and saves each on/off switch, showing a message if saving fails. Switches stay clickable while saving. Calls the notifications API; used by Kinds.
Generates a random private ntfy topic name, 'jechel-' followed by 12 hex characters. Anyone who knows the name can read its messages. Used by the Connections section of Settings.
Tracks whether a service card is expanded, gives it a stable id, and turns its status into display text (none for link-only services). Makes no API calls; used by ServiceCard in Settings.

Manages a settings field's draft value, saving or removing it through the settings API and showing saved or error text. Secret values are never shown, and removal is allowed only for values stored in settings. Used by SettingField.
Loads all connection settings from the store and looks them up by key, with a ready, partial, or off status for each service. Used by the Connections section of the Settings page.

Runs a connection test for one service through the settings API and tracks whether it is busy and what the result was. Used by the Settings page's TestButton, and shows a generic failure message if the test call errors.
Loads the terms and lets a signed-in admin edit a draft and save it through the terms API. Saving shows the new terms to all visitors on the Terms page and asks them to accept again.

Runs the unsubscribe action for the address in the email link and turns its state into a status message: working, done, test email, incomplete link, or failure. Used by the UnsubscribePage in the updates feature.
Fetches the newest app or video, limited to the sections visitors may see per site settings, and waits until those settings load. Tells the admin when content is hidden. Used by the WhatsNew page.
Supplies the page text, a key for each video, and a refresh option that is enabled only when the user is signed in. Used by the YouTube page, which takes its sign-in state from the auth hook.

frontend-views:module:frontend/src/main..text: Application entry point that mounts the React tree, creating the store, applying the theme and global styles, and starting the idle watcher. Loaded by index.html as the page's script.

frontend-views:symbol:frontend/src/App/A.text: Top-level router that defines all site routes inside a shared layout, gates public pages behind visibility settings, and shows a downtime layout during maintenance. Mounted by main.tsx.

frontend-views:symbol:frontend/src/auth/.text: Renders its children only when the admin is signed in, passing the signed-in user to function children, and renders nothing while auth is loading. Used on the Contact page for admin-only content.
Renders its children only when nobody is signed in, and renders nothing while auth is loading. Used on the Contact page for content meant for anonymous visitors.

frontend-views:symbol:frontend/src/compo.text: Wrapper for admin-only pages. It shows a skeleton while the session loads, sends anonymous visitors to the home page, and otherwise renders its children. Used by the Community, Engagement, Feature Testing, Notifications, and Settings pages.

Modal that asks the user to confirm an action, with Cancel focused by default so an accidental Enter does nothing. It shows a working state while confirming and an error alert on failure. Used by DeleteButton, DiscardChangesDialog, and MeetingActions.

Icon button that copies a value to the clipboard. It announces the result to screen readers and switches icons to show success or failure. Used in the About, Analytics, YouTube, and Settings views, and in contact details.

Trash icon button that opens a ConfirmDialog before calling onDelete. The item name, action label, and detail text are configurable. Used in many places, including About, Apps, Contact, Notifications, Updates, and Analytics.

Confirmation shown when a popup has unsaved changes. Discard calls onDiscard, and Cancel returns to the editor. Built on ConfirmDialog and used by the Apps dialogs AppDialog, CategoriesDialog, and OrganiseDialog.

Placeholder for lists with nothing in them, showing an icon, a message that defaults to 'Nothing here yet', and an optional hint. Used by the Updates, Support, Feature Testing, and Notifications views.

Shared display for data that failed to load. It shows an alert with the error message and an optional Try again button. Used across About, Analytics, Apps, Auth, Contact, Meetings, Notifications, Resume, and the shared PagedGrid.
Small secondary button with a plus icon and a label such as 'Add …', shown under editable lists in the About, Apps and Terms editors. Calls its onClick handler when pressed.
Fieldset of checkboxes for choosing several items from a fixed set, such as what a skill was used for. Shows an optional colour swatch and error message. Used by PeriodEditor and ResumePanel.
Colour input that opens the browser's colour picker and stores a '#rrggbb' value, with label and optional error. Used by ColorsFieldset in the About section.

Move-up, move-down and remove controls for one entry in an editable list. Move buttons appear only when a move handler is given, and removal asks for confirmation first. Used across About, Apps and Terms editors.
'Add link' control for text fields: asks for link text and URL, then inserts Markdown [text](url) over the selection or at the cursor. Used by TextField in the About section.

Month-and-year input built from a month dropdown and a year box, since some browsers lack a native month picker. Stores the value as 'YYYY-MM-01'. Used by QualificationEditor, PeriodEditor and TimelineEntryEditor.

Labelled text input or textarea with optional hint, error, suggestions datalist, and an Add link helper. Used by most editor forms (hackathons, languages, papers, profile, skills, timeline entries and others) and wraps a view-model hook for ids and refs.

Shows an image whole inside a fixed frame, with a blurred, enlarged copy behind it to fill the empty space. The frame size comes from CSS. Used by the Apps MediaCard, MediaSlide, and MediaThumbnail components.
Down-chevron SVG icon built on the shared Icon component. Used in item controls, section headers, the skill editor, and the settings service card.
Left-chevron SVG icon built on the shared Icon component. Used by the apps carousel controls, the meetings calendar, and the auth tab navigation.
Right-chevron SVG icon built on the shared Icon component. Used by the apps carousel controls, the meetings calendar, and the auth tab navigation.
Up-chevron SVG icon built on the shared Icon component. Used only by the item controls in the about feature for reordering items.
Two circular arrows icon signifying a self-running process, built on the shared Icon component. Currently not used by any component; intended for Work with me automations.
ID-card style SVG icon with a photo circle and text lines, built on the shared Icon component. Currently not used anywhere in the codebase.
Bell icon split into body and clapper parts that animate a ring on hover. Used by the SubscribeButton in the updates feature, where hovering the Get updates button rings it.
Boat-on-water SVG icon built on the shared Icon component. Currently not used by any component.
Shared SVG wrapper for brand logos that sets size and hides it from screen readers. Used by the GitHub, Instagram, LinkedIn, LeetCode, and YouTube icons.
Outline car icon, a simple line drawing with two wheels and a body. Shared by the app; no callers are recorded in the map.
Checkmark icon used for confirmation states. Rendered by NeetCodeLists, CurrencyPicker, and RefreshVideosButton; wraps the shared Icon component.
Downward chevron icon, used as a dropdown indicator. Rendered by CurrencyPicker in the workwithme feature; wraps the shared Icon component.
Clipboard icon with a checkmark, shown after content is copied. Used by CopyButton; wraps the shared Icon component.
Plain clipboard icon for copy actions. Used by CopyButton; wraps the shared Icon component.
Clipboard icon with an X, shown when a copy fails. Used by CopyButton; wraps the shared Icon component.
X icon used to dismiss or close UI. Rendered by PlacePopup in the about feature and RefreshVideosButton in youtube; wraps the shared Icon component.
Angle-bracket code icon. No callers are recorded in the map; wraps the shared Icon component.
Coffee cup icon with animated steam that fills with coffee on hover of the Buy me a coffee button. Used by SupportButton in the support feature; calls useCoffeeIconViewModel for its clip-path id.
Shared download icon, an SVG tray with a down arrow, built on the common Icon component. Used by PaperItem in the about feature and ResumeDownloads in the resume feature.
Expand icon: an SVG of diagonal arrows pointing outward from corners. Used by ZoomControls in the about feature to show a fullscreen or enlarge action.
External-link icon: a box with an arrow leaving it. Shared icon used by StoreLinks (apps), VideoDetailsView (youtube), and ServiceCard (settings) to mark links that open elsewhere.
Eye icon: an open eye, drawn with two classed paths. Shared icon used by ContentToggle to show content as visible.
Crossed-out eye icon: a closed eye with a slash through it. Shared icon used by ContentToggle to show hidden content and by TabLink in auth.
Lab flask icon marking features being tried out. Used by FeatureTesting in the featuretesting feature.
GitHub logo built on BrandIcon, filled with currentColor so it shows black on light and white on dark backgrounds. Not currently used by any component.
Globe icon for websites, drawn as a circle with meridian and equator lines. Not currently used by any component, though its doc comment says it represents websites in Work with me.
Six-dot grip handle used for drag-to-reorder. Used by MediaListEditor and OrganiseDialog in the apps feature.

Base SVG wrapper for all icons: 24×24 line style, currentColor, 18px default size, hidden from screen readers. Used by most icon components across the app; callers must label the surrounding button or link.
Picture icon: a framed image with a sun and mountain outline. Used by MediaCard in the apps feature to represent images.
Stroked inbox tray icon, a shared SVG glyph built on the generic Icon wrapper. Rendered by EmptyState to show an empty-inbox placeholder.
Instagram camera glyph filled with a radial yellow-to-purple gradient. Gets its gradient ID from useInstagramIconViewModel and wraps BrandIcon; no current callers.
LeetCode logo in its orange brand color, drawn as a fixed SVG path inside BrandIcon. Used by LeetCodeProfileLink in the about feature.
LinkedIn logo with a white rounded square and blue 'in' mark, built on BrandIcon. Has no current callers in the codebase.
Chain-link icon drawn with two stroked paths over the shared Icon wrapper. Used by LinkInserter in the about feature to show link insertion.
Single horizontal-line minus icon over the shared Icon wrapper. Used by ZoomControls in the about feature for zoom-out.
Crescent moon icon for dark-mode toggles, drawn as one path over the shared Icon wrapper. Has no current callers in the codebase.

Pencil edit icon built from two stroked paths over the shared Icon wrapper. Shared by six components, including PlacesList, SectionHeader, AppDialog, UpdateEmailsEditor, WorkWithMePrice and TermsPage.
Person silhouette icon with a head circle and shoulder arc, drawn at 1.5 stroke width. Used by ProfilePhoto in the about feature as a placeholder avatar.
Mobile phone outline with a speaker bar, drawn over the shared Icon wrapper. Used by PrivateContact in about and ResumeDownloads in resume.
Renders an airplane SVG icon by wrapping the shared Icon component with a plane path. Not currently imported by any other component.
Renders a play-triangle SVG icon via the shared Icon wrapper. Used by MediaSlide and MediaThumbnail in the apps feature to mark playable media.
Renders a plus-sign SVG icon via the shared Icon wrapper. Used by AddButton and ZoomControls in the about feature, and AddAppTile in apps, for add actions.
Renders a circular-arrow refresh SVG icon via the shared Icon wrapper. Used by RefreshVideosButton in the youtube feature.
Renders a magnifying-glass SVG icon via the shared Icon wrapper. Used by CitySearch in the about feature.
Renders a sort-arrows SVG icon via the shared Icon wrapper. Used by SortableListHeader in the about feature to indicate sortable columns.
Renders a five-point star SVG icon via the shared Icon wrapper. Used by CurrencyPicker in the workwithme feature, likely for favorite or selected currencies.
Renders a sun SVG icon with animatable rays (class sun-rays) via the shared Icon wrapper. Not currently imported by any other component.

Renders a trash-can SVG icon via the shared Icon wrapper. Used for delete actions in DeleteButton (shared), FileUpload and PlacesList (about), VisitView (analytics), AppForm (apps), and MessageDialog (contact).
Renders an upload-arrow SVG icon via the shared Icon wrapper. Used by FileUpload in the about feature and MediaListEditor in apps.
Renders the red YouTube play-button brand icon by wrapping the shared BrandIcon with two SVG paths. Only YouTubeChannelButton in the youtube feature uses it.
Renders plain text with any web addresses turned into links that open in a new tab. Used by VideoDetailsView in the YouTube feature to display video descriptions.
Card with an image, title, optional meta line, and description. The title link stretches over the whole card, so the entire card is clickable. Used by the Apps AppTile and the YouTube VideoTile.

Accessible dialog rendered into the document body. Traps focus while open, closes on Escape or backdrop click unless non-dismissible, and restores focus to the opener. Used by many feature dialogs across the app.
On/Off toggle styled like the theme switcher, with a sliding thumb. Built on hidden radio buttons so arrow keys work. Used in app forms, the organise dialog, and notification settings.

Three-column grid showing one page at a time with Previous/Next, storing the page in the URL. Animates page changes, handles loading, error, and empty states, and prefetches neighbouring pages. Used by the Apps and YouTube pages.

Previous / 'Page X of Y' / Next controls. Renders nothing when there is only one page. Used by PagedGrid and several tables and lists including visits, messages, announcements, donations, subscribers, and history.

Live region that announces a label to screen readers and wraps placeholder shapes hidden from them. Used across many pages and dialogs while content loads, including PagedGrid and the meetings calendar.
Full-page loading placeholder showing two skeleton cards, used while the session is being checked. Wrapped in the shared Loading region. Used by AdminOnly and the site's visible-page wrapper.
Basic shimmering placeholder block with configurable width, height, and radius. Used as the building block for the other skeleton components across the app, instead of spinners.
Placeholder card with an optional heading bar and a paragraph of text lines. Used for the About page skeleton and inside the full-page skeleton shown during session checks.
Row of rounded placeholder pills, sized to look like chips or checkboxes. Used in the About and resume skeletons and the visit dialog while loading.
Placeholder list rows, each with a short label bar and a longer line, optionally with a pill. Used while loading emails, settings, visit steps, the meetings calendar, and history.
Loading placeholder grid of media cards (16:9 image, title, line, short description) shown while Apps and YouTube items load. Built from Skeleton and SkeletonText; rendered by PagedGrid.
Loading placeholder for table rows: a header plus configurable rows and columns of grey bars. Used while the analytics visits table, contact inbox, donations, and subscribers load.
Loading placeholder for a paragraph: a set number of grey text lines, with the last line shorter. Used in SkeletonCard, SkeletonMediaGrid, MessageDialog, TermsSkeleton and WhatsNewSkeleton.
Decorative 'Vice' wordmark with an animated neon-sunset gradient, sized for the theme switch. Hidden from screen readers, and marked so browser translators leave the name unchanged.

frontend-views:symbol:frontend/src/featu.text: Loading placeholder for the About page: a profile-card skeleton with photo, name, and chip rows, followed by three section-card skeletons. AboutPage shows it while data loads.
Labeled file field with Upload/Replace and optional Remove buttons. It uploads immediately, but the page only uses the file after its section is saved. PaperEditor and ProfileEditor use it.
Shows a small country flag image for a code, or nothing when there is no flag. It is decorative, with a title from flagName. StatusChips, StatusEditor, and workwithme's CurrencyFlag use it.
Editor for one hackathon with a name field, a validated four-digit year, a bullet list of what happened, and move and remove controls. HackathonsEditor renders one per row.
Editor list for all hackathons, with a sortable header, one HackathonEditor per row, a list-level error, and an add button that puts new entries at the top. HackathonsSection hosts it.
About page section that shows hackathons as a timeline, with a muted placeholder when the list is empty. When editable, it switches to HackathonsEditor and saves through onSave. AboutPage uses it.
Inline editor row for one spoken language, with a name field, a level dropdown, and move and remove controls. LanguagesEditor renders one per language.
Renders one language in the About page's list: its name, a row of step dots showing proficiency (filled ones lit), and the level as text. Used by LanguagesSection; takes a LanguageView.

Editor for the languages list in the About section, showing one row per language that can be reordered, plus an Add language button and a list-level error. Used by LanguagesSection; uses useLanguagesEditorViewModel.

The Languages block on the About page: shows each language with its level, or 'Nothing here yet' when empty, and wraps it in an editable section that saves through onSave. Used by AboutPage; uses LanguageItem and LanguagesEditor.
Decorative icon for a licence category: car, plane, boat, or a generic badge for other kinds. Takes a category and optional size. Used by LicenceGroup and OfferedLicences.
Display block for one licence category on the About page: a heading with its icon and label, and the licences listed as chips. Used by LicencesSection; renders LicenceLabel for each entry.
Shows a licence's text: the code in bold when present, followed by the name describing what it's for. Used by LicenceGroup and OwnLicences; has no outgoing dependencies.

Editor for licences in the About section: toggle buttons for offered driving, flying and boating licences, plus an 'Others' fieldset for custom licences and a form to add them. Used by LicencesSection.

The Licences block on the About page: driving, flying and boating licences grouped by kind as labels, or 'Nothing here yet' when empty, wrapped in an editable section saving through onSave. Used by AboutPage; uses LicenceGroup and LicencesEditor.
Fieldset for one licence category in the licence editor, with a toggle button per offered licence showing its code and name and its pressed state. Used by LicencesEditor; uses LicenceCategoryIcon.

Form for adding a licence that isn't in the offered list: pick a kind, enter an optional code and a name, then add it. Used by LicencesEditor; uses TextField, AddButton and useOwnLicenceFormViewModel.
Lists the licences the admin added by hand, each with its kind, any error, and a remove control. Renders nothing when there are none. Used by LicencesEditor.
Editor for one paper: its title field and PDF upload, plus move and remove controls. Used by PapersEditor. Uploading a PDF makes the title link to it.
Displays one paper. If it has a PDF, the title is a download link; otherwise the title is shown as rich text with its links. Used by PapersSection.
Editor for the full paper list: one PaperEditor per paper, reorderable, with list-level error display and an Add paper button. Used by PapersSection.
The 'Academic papers' section on the About page. Shows each paper as a download link or plain title, or 'Nothing here yet' when empty. Editable by users who can edit, saving via onSave.
Lists city search matches as buttons; clicking one places that city via onPick. Shows 'No places found' when the list is empty. Used by CitySearch.
Search box for adding a city to the map. Shows searching and error states and the matching results, with GeoNames credited. Picking a result calls onPick. Used by PlacesEditor.
Draws a map pin as a single-colour dot, or as equal pie-slice segments clockwise from the top for multiple colours, with an outline. Used by WorldMap.
Decorative ring drawn around a city being added so it stands out on the world map. Hidden from screen readers. Used by WorldMap.
Tooltip-style card for a map pin showing the place name and a list of its visits, each with a colour swatch and note or label. Stays open while hovered. Used by WorldMap.

Dialog shown over the map for one place, with checkboxes for worked, studied, and visited, each with an optional note that can hold links. Used by PlacesEditor; it has a close button and a Remove action.
Admin editor for the Where I've been section: colour settings, a city search, the clickable world map with the place popup, and the places list. Rendered by PlacesSection.
Lists the mapped places with their colour dots, visit types, and Edit and Remove buttons. Renders nothing when there are no places. Used by PlacesEditor.

The public 'Where I've been' section of the About page, showing a colour legend, a dotted world map with pins, and a 'No places yet' note when empty. Editable through PlacesEditor and saved via onSave.
SVG dotted world map that draws a coloured pin per place, with hover, focus, and tap details, plus zoom and drag. Uses MapPin, PlaceCard, and ZoomControls. Used by PlacesSection and PlacesEditor.
Corner buttons for zooming in, zooming out, and resetting the world map view, with buttons disabled when the zoom limit is reached. Rendered by WorldMap.
List of LeetCode problems solved out of the total for each difficulty, each with a progress bar. Rendered by LeetCodeCard.
Shows a user's LeetCode stats: a profile link, a solved-count ring, and per-difficulty breakdown, with loading, error, and not-found states. Keyed by username; used by ProblemSolvingSection.
Link showing the LeetCode icon and @username that opens the profile on LeetCode in a new tab. Rendered by LeetCodeCard.
Loading placeholder for the LeetCode stats, with a circular ring block and three text lines, labelled 'Loading LeetCode stats'. Rendered by LeetCodeCard while data loads.
Renders the list of NeetCode lists the owner has completed, as checkmarked chips. Shown inside the Problem solving section when at least one list is set.
Edit form for the Problem solving section: a LeetCode username field and toggle buttons for each NeetCode list. Built on the shared editor view model hook.
About-page section showing LeetCode stats and completed NeetCode lists, with an empty state. Wraps its content in EditableSection and uses ProblemSolvingEditor for editing.
SVG ring showing the total LeetCode problems solved, with arcs split by difficulty. Takes the solved counts from LeetCodeStats and computes the arcs in its view model hook.
Admin-only block listing the owner's email and phone (the résumé header), each with a copy button. Visitors never see it; an empty-text message shows when no items exist.
Edit form for the profile section: photo upload, admin-only résumé contact fields, citizenship/residence statuses, and GitHub, LinkedIn and Instagram URLs. Uses the profile editor view model.
Renders the profile's links as secondary buttons with icons. Download links get the download attribute, and external links open in a new tab with safe rel attributes.
Shows the profile photo as an image, or a person-icon placeholder when no URL is set. Expects the URL to have already passed the isSafeUrl check.
About-page card with the photo, name, headline, citizenship/residence chips and links. Shows admin-only private contact details and a retryable error state, and uses ProfileEditor for editing.
Lists the citizenship and residence labels under the photo, each with its flag and rich text. Shows an empty-state hint when none exist and the caller asks for it.
Editor for one profile label under the photo: a flag dropdown, a required text field, and move/remove controls. Rendered in a group by StatusesEditor, and uses useStatusEditorViewModel for state.
Editor for the list of profile labels under the photo, rendering one StatusEditor per row with an Add label button and list-level error display. Used by ProfileEditor in the about feature.
Form fieldset for one qualification, with title, issuer, obtained month, and optional grade, plus move/remove controls. Rendered by QualificationsEditor and driven by its view model.
Read-only list item showing a qualification's title, issuer, obtained date, and grade, with rich-text links and only the fields that are present. Rendered inside QualificationsSection.
Editor for the full qualifications list, rendering a QualificationEditor per row with reorder support, list errors, and an Add qualification button. Passed to QualificationsSection as its editor.

About page section for certifications, shown as an editable block with a 'Nothing here yet' placeholder when empty. Lists items via QualificationItem and saves through QualificationsEditor. Used by AboutPage.

Renders a link as an in-app router link for site pages, or as a plain anchor otherwise. Non-root links open in a new tab with noopener noreferrer. It expects an href already checked by isSafeUrl. RichText uses it.
Renders text containing [text](url) links as real links, using parseRichText and ExternalLink. Used throughout about, in apps' AppDetailsView, and in the terms document views.
Renders a bulleted list of rich-text strings, returning nothing when the list is empty. Used by TimelineItem in the about feature to show entry bullet points.

Generic editor for a list of strings, showing one text field per bullet with reorder and remove controls and an add button. Empty bullets are dropped on save. Used by HackathonEditor, TimelineEntryEditor, and terms' SectionEditor.
Legend listing colour swatches with labels, using round dots for map pins and an optional hint line. Used by PlacesSection and SkillsChart in the about feature.
Renders a "Colours" fieldset holding one colour picker per colour choice. Used by the About page's PlacesEditor and SkillsEditor to set colours for each skill or visit kind.
Wrapper for every About Me section: shows a header and a collapsible body, and swaps the body for an edit form when the admin clicks Edit. Used by all About section components.
The edit-mode form for a section: renders the section's editor, an alert with the save error if any, and Save and Cancel buttons. Rendered by EditableSection.
Header bar for an About section: the title, plus an admin-only Edit button and a collapse/expand toggle. Rendered by EditableSection.
Sort button shown above reorderable lists in the About editors, with a status message announced to screen readers after sorting. Used by the Hackathons, Skills and Timeline editors.
Editor for one usage period of a skill: start month, end month or a 'still using it' checkbox, and which uses apply. Rendered inside SkillEditor.
One coloured bar on the skills timeline for a usage period, with a tooltip showing the skill, use and dates on hover or focus. Rendered by SkillsChart.
Collapsible editor for one skill: name, its usage periods, and move/remove controls. Starts folded unless it has an error. Rendered by SkillsEditor.
Public timeline of skills, one row per skill with coloured bars for each usage period, a year axis, a legend and total experience. Rendered by SkillsSection.
Admin editor for the Skills section: colour settings for each use, a sortable and reorderable list of SkillEditor rows, and an Add skill button. Passed to EditableSection by SkillsSection.
The Skills block on the About Me page: shows the skills timeline, or 'No skills yet' when empty, and wires in the editor and save handler. Rendered by AboutPage.
Editor for education entries on the About page. It wraps the shared TimelineEditor with the education config and is rendered by EducationSection.
Renders the education timeline on the About page, switching into EducationEditor when editing is allowed. Receives its entries and save handler from AboutPage.
Editor for work experience entries on the About page. It wraps the shared TimelineEditor with the experience config and is rendered by ExperienceSection.
Renders the work experience timeline on the About page, switching into ExperienceEditor when editing is allowed. Receives its entries and save handler from AboutPage.
Shared list editor for timeline entries, letting the user reorder, sort, add, and remove them, with new entries placed on top. Used by the education and experience editors.
Form for one timeline entry: title, organization, location, start and end months, an ongoing toggle, and optional bullet points for work. Rendered once per entry by TimelineEditor.
Read-only display of one timeline entry, showing title, an optional Upcoming tag, meta info, period, and bullets. Used by TimelineSection and HackathonsSection.
Shared read-only timeline section that lists entries newest first inside an editable wrapper, showing a placeholder when empty. Used by the education and experience sections.
A 'Sign in with Google' link button with Google's logo, pointing to the API's sign-in URL, which redirects back to the frontend. Rendered by AdminPage.
Loading placeholder shaped like the sign-in card, shown while the session is being checked. Built from shared Loading and Skeleton components and rendered by AdminPage.
Renders nothing; passes page opens, theme switches and visitor info to the analytics Tracker, skipping the admin. Mounted once in the site App.
Titled top-10 list of name and count rows, each with a bar scaled to the largest count. Shows an empty message when there are no items. Used on the analytics Dashboard.

Responsive column chart of one measure at a time, with buttons to switch metric and hover or tap tooltips per day. A hidden table gives screen readers the same numbers. Used on the analytics Dashboard.
Six headline analytics tiles for the period: visitors, visits, page views, average visit, bounce rate and errors. The errors tile is highlighted when errors exist. Used on the Dashboard.
Small label-and-value pair rendered as a definition list entry. Used inside VisitView to show device, window, theme and similar visit facts.
Modal that loads one visit by id and shows loading, error or the replayed visit. Supports closing and deleting the visit. Opened from VisitsTable rows.
Shows a visit's device, window, theme, length, referrer and location, then its ordered event timeline with expandable error details. Offers copy-as-steps and delete actions.
Paginated table of visits, newest first, with an errors-only filter. Clicking a row or start time opens the VisitDialog timeline. Used on the analytics Dashboard.
Admin-only tile at the start of the Apps grid labelled 'Add an app'. Clicking it calls onAdd, which opens an empty app popup. Used by AppsPage.
Shows an app's media carousel, rich-text description, platform chips and store links, with optional extra children. Used in the AppDialog popup and on the What's new page.

The popup for one app. Shows its media slider, title and description, with an Edit button for admins; new apps open straight into the form. Built on AppDetailsView, AppForm and the discard-changes prompt.
Header bar of the app popup: the title, with the app's category labels shown beneath it while viewing, and a close button. Rendered by AppDialog.

The admin's form for editing an app: title, categories, What's new visibility, description, platforms, links, and media. Ends with Delete (for saved apps), Cancel and Save; API errors show under the fields.
One card on the Apps grid, showing the app's picture, title, category labels and start of its description. Clicking it opens the app's popup via AppDialog.
Controls under the media slides: previous and next buttons, a dot per slide, and a live slide counter. Disabled buttons reflect whether you can go back or forward. Used by MediaCarousel.
Admin-only Categories button above the Apps grid. Opens the CategoriesDialog for editing the category list and closes it once saved or cancelled.
Popup where admins rename, reorder, add and remove app categories, saved all at once. Removing a category removes it from every app. Warns before discarding unsaved changes.
Renders an app's categories as small text labels, and renders nothing when the app has none. Used by AppTile, AppDialogHeader and LatestApp in the What's new feature.
Toggle buttons inside AppForm for choosing an app's categories, in the saved category order. Shows a hint to add categories first when none exist yet.
One row in the CategoriesDialog list: a text field for the category name, plus move and remove controls. Rendered inside an ordered list by CategoriesDialog.
Form section where an admin adds, edits and removes an app's 'Check it on' links, each a store name plus its URL. Rendered inside AppForm; state comes from useLinksEditorViewModel.
Swipeable, keyboard-navigable carousel of an app's images and videos, shown on AppDetailsView. Renders nothing when there are no slides; delegates each slide to MediaSlide.
Admin editor for an app's media: drag-to-reorder list, file uploads (saved immediately), and adding YouTube or other links. Rendered inside AppForm and driven by useMediaListEditorViewModel.
Renders one carousel slide as an image, a native video, a YouTube player, or a clickable thumbnail that loads the player on demand. Used only by MediaCarousel.
Small preview tile for one app media item in the MediaListEditor list, with a play icon on videos. Picks image, YouTube thumbnail, or video preview based on the item's kind.
Admin-only 'Organise' button shown above the Apps grid on AppsPage. Opens the OrganiseDialog when clicked.
Modal where an admin drags apps into display order and toggles each one's What's new? visibility, then saves. Asks before discarding unsaved changes; state comes from useOrganiseDialogViewModel.
Shows a 'Runs on' label with the app's platforms as chips on AppDetailsView. Renders nothing if the app lists no platforms.
Admin form section for an app's platforms: toggle buttons for common ones plus a text field to add others. Rendered inside AppForm and driven by usePlatformsEditorViewModel.
Renders the app's store links as 'Check it on' buttons that open in a new tab on AppDetailsView. Renders nothing when there are no safe links.

Settings section listing each device signed in as the admin, with browser, address, sign-in and activity times, and expiry. Lets the admin sign out one device or all the others. Uses the auth view model and is rendered by SettingsPage.

Public 'Contact me' form. Send stays disabled until every field is valid, and errors show once a field is left. Shows a topic picker when enabled, and success, failure, or rate-limit states. Uses the contact form view model and is rendered by ContactPage.
Small helper that shows a field's error message under its input, or renders nothing when there is no error. Used only by ContactForm.
One label and value row in a message's details list. Emails become mailto links, and each value gets a copy button. Used by MessageDialog for name, email, received time, subject, and message body.

Modal showing one contact message: sender details, meetings they booked, the reply conversation, and a delete button. Opening it marks the message as read. Opened from MessagesInbox and uses the message dialog view model.

Conversation section inside the message dialog. Shows earlier replies oldest first, plus a form to email the admin's next reply to the sender, with an optional booking-link insert. Uses the replies view model.

Admin's contact-form inbox: a paginated table of 10 messages per page, newest first, with unread markers, project-enquiry tags, and per-row delete. Clicking a name opens MessageDialog. Rendered by ContactPage.

Accepts or declines a requested meeting with an optional message emailed to the attendee; declines also pass the reason to Cal.com. Accepted meetings that haven't ended can be cancelled after confirmation. Used by MessageDialog and MeetingsCalendar.

Admin's Cal.com meetings view on ContactPage: a month calendar with status dots per day, the selected day's meetings below, and a count of pending requests. Each meeting renders MeetingActions for accept, decline, or cancel.

First card on the Notifications page. Toggles ntfy and site notifications on or off, and lists devices receiving site notifications, each with send-test and remove actions. Also offers to allow notifications on this device. Uses the alert channels view model.
Shows this browser's push-notification status in the alerts card: a button to allow them, a note to turn them on in iPhone settings or via Home Screen, or that the browser can't get them at all.
Admin-only three-way radio slider in the admin bar for previewing the site as normal, loading, or failed. Driven by usePreviewSwitchViewModel; rendered by AdminBar.
Shows when the résumés were last generated and two download links: the private copy with email and phone, and the public copy. Shows 'Not generated yet' if none exists. Used by ResumePanel.
Admin-only résumé generator on the About Me page, where the admin picks sections and skills, saves, and generates the public and private PDFs. Uses useResumePanelViewModel and embeds ResumeDownloads.
Placeholder shown in ResumePanel while résumé settings load: a title line, eight section chips, and a button outline. Built from shared Loading and Skeleton components.
Static 'Coming soon' card shown to visitors when every visitor page is switched off. Rendered by App; takes no data and calls nothing.
Screen shown in the site frame when maintenance mode is on or the API is unreachable, with a title, text, and a Try again button. Uses useMaintenanceScreenViewModel; AppLayout renders it as downtime.

Settings panel where the admin switches each visitor page, feature, and maintenance mode on or off, each saving immediately, plus an optional maintenance message. Used by SettingsPage; backed by useSiteVisibilityViewModel.
Reusable on/off toggle button with role=switch, showing a label, optional note, and busy state. Rendered for each row in SiteVisibility; state comes from SwitchItem and useSwitchViewModel.
Route wrapper that shows its child page if visitors may see it, otherwise redirects to the first visible page or Coming soon. Shows PageSkeleton while visibility loads; used by App.
Header "Buy me a coffee" link that opens the donation page URL from the API's Support:Url setting in a new tab. Shows a skeleton while loading, and renders nothing if no URL is set.
Fieldset of checkboxes that a visitor ticks to confirm each consent statement before using the site. Used by the welcome gate to collect acceptance of the terms.
Modal popup showing the terms, with loading, error (with retry), and loaded states. Closes via the × button, Escape, or an outside click, and sits above other popups including the welcome gate.
Renders the terms as an article: optional title, updated date, introduction, then numbered sections. Used by the terms dialog and the terms page.
Admin form for one terms section: heading, reorder and remove controls, and an editable list of paragraph and bullet-list blocks with add buttons. Used by TermsEditor.
Admin form for editing the whole terms document: title, optional introduction, and a list of sections with add controls. Used by the terms page, with validation errors passed in.
Non-dismissable welcome popup requiring visitors to tick every consent and press Continue. Offers a link that opens the full terms above it. Shown by TermsHost to visitors who must accept.
Top-level host mounted in App that shows the welcome gate to visitors who still must accept the terms (not the signed-in admin), and the terms dialog when opened on request.
Renders one numbered terms section: its heading followed by paragraphs and bullet lists, with inline rich text and links. Used by TermsDocumentView.
Loading placeholder shaped like the terms: an introduction block followed by three numbered section placeholders. Shown inside the terms dialog and terms page while content loads.
Header "Get updates" button in the updates feature. Clicking it opens the SubscribeDialog modal; it has no data of its own and is rendered by AppLayout.

Modal for email signup, rendered by SubscribeButton. It shows SubscribeForm until submission, then SubscribeSent, and its state comes from useSubscribeDialogViewModel. Signup uses double opt-in, so a confirmation email is sent.

Form inside SubscribeDialog with an email input and submit button, plus a short explanation of the updates. All values and handlers come in as props from the dialog's view model, and it shows validation and failure messages.
Confirmation panel shown in SubscribeDialog after submission. It tells the user to check their email, or that the address is already subscribed, and includes a Done button that closes the dialog.
Internal helper rendering the four text fields (subject, message, button, note) for one email kind in UpdateEmailsEditor. Changes are passed up through onChange, and errors are shown per field.

Community tab editor for the subscriber emails. It shows a live preview in a sandboxed, inert iframe, with Edit, Save, Cancel and a "Send me a test" action that goes to the admin's inbox. Data and actions come from useUpdateEmailsEditorViewModel; it is used by CommunityPage.

Shared card shown on the email-link landing pages (confirm subscription and unsubscribe). It displays a status message, a link back to the home page, and optional extra action buttons; it is used by ConfirmSubscriptionPage and UnsubscribePage.
Full display of the newest app on the What's New page. It wraps AppDetailsView in WhatsNewCard, adds category labels, and gets its view state from useLatestAppViewModel. Used by WhatsNewPage.

Shows the newest YouTube video on the What's New page, with the player and description via VideoDetailsView inside WhatsNewCard. It gets its state from useLatestVideoViewModel and is used by WhatsNewPage.
Shared article card for the newest app or video on What's New. It shows the kind, date, title and category labels in a header, then renders its children. Used by LatestApp and LatestVideo.
Loading placeholder for the newest What's New item, matching its kind and date line, title, picture, and description. WhatsNewPage shows it while the content loads.
Small decorative flag icon for a currency, drawn from its flag code. It's hidden from screen readers because the code and name beside it already identify the currency. Used by CurrencyPicker.

Dropdown for picking a currency, listing favourites EUR, RON and GBP first, then the rest, each with flag, code and name. Its state and keyboard handling come from a view model. WorkWithMePrice uses it in the admin price editor.
The Work With Me section: services offered, the steps of a project, and the price. It renders WorkWithMePrice at the bottom.
Shows the hourly rate to visitors, read-only. The signed-in admin gets an edit form for currency and amount. The API's default of €25 applies until a price is set. Used by WorkWithMe.

Admin button that fetches YouTube videos immediately, for example after an upload, instead of waiting for the hourly refresh. Its icon spins, then shows a green tick, or a red cross with a copyable error dialog.
Shows one YouTube video: the privacy-enhanced player, the full description with links, and a Watch on YouTube link. LatestVideo in the What's New feature renders it.
Grid card for a YouTube video showing its thumbnail, title, date, and description excerpt. Clicking it opens the video on YouTube. Built on the shared MediaCard and used on the YouTube page.
Button that opens the owner's YouTube channel in a new tab. It renders nothing while loading or when no channel is set in Settings → YouTube. Used on the confirm-subscription and YouTube pages.
Embeds YouTube's privacy-enhanced player as an iframe for a given embed URL, optionally loaded lazily. Used by VideoDetailsView and by MediaSlide in the apps feature.

frontend-views:symbol:frontend/src/layou.text: Admin-only bar above the header showing an Admin badge, maintenance warning link, preview switch (in development), signed-in user, and a Sign out button. Renders nothing for visitors.

Site frame wrapping every page: header with admin bar, brand, support/updates buttons, theme switch and tabs, then the page, footer, and Vice-only scene elements. In downtime, shows the maintenance screen inside the same frame.

The animated Riviera scene behind the site when the Vice theme is active, drawn on a WebGL canvas. It falls back to a still image where WebGL 2 is unavailable or the scene fails. Purely decorative and hidden from assistive tech.
The site name 'jechel.dev' as a home link in the top header. In Vice theme it renders as neon text with decorative layers hidden from screen readers.
Draws the 'j' in the site name for the Vice theme, where CSS replaces the letter with a custom-drawn glyph while keeping the text for screen readers and search.
Vice-only button that hides the page so only the Riviera scene shows. The button fades when idle and returns on mouse movement; Escape also restores the page.
Renders the current tab's page and animates tab switches as a sideways slide, keeping the outgoing page mounted and inert until its animation ends.
Footer pill showing the copyright year and a Terms and Conditions link that opens in a popup. Hidden while the welcome popup is open.
Status message shown when the theme changes because Vice was too slow for the device, with buttons to keep Vice anyway or dismiss it.
Pill-style navigation row for the admin's System pages, shown above the page content when the System tab is active. Displays optional badges per page.

Single tab link in the main navigation, marked current when active. Admin-only tabs get a pink/violet style, hidden-from-visitor tabs get an eye-off icon, and an optional badge like BETA follows the label.

The main section tab bar, rendered by AppLayout. Admin-only tabs appear after sign-in, the current tab is marked, and a sliding highlight can be dragged to snap to the nearest tab. Edge arrows scroll the bar on pointer devices.

A three-way picker for the dark, light and Vice colour themes, rendered by AppLayout. Built on radio inputs so arrow keys work, with a sliding thumb under the chosen option. Logic comes from useThemeSwitchViewModel.

A development-only bar above the header, shown only when running locally. It has a Reset terms acceptance button so the welcome popup can be seen again. Rendered by AppLayout, with logic from useUserBarViewModel.

frontend-views:symbol:frontend/src/pages.text: The public About Me page, built from sections for profile, places, problem solving, skills, experience, education, papers, qualifications, languages, licences and hackathons. Admins also get a resume panel and can edit every section.

The admin sign-in page, offering only Google sign-in. Already-signed-in users are redirected home, and a failed attempt shows an error message. State comes from useAdminPageViewModel in the auth feature.

The Apps page, showing the owner's apps in a paged grid in their saved order. Tapping a tile opens its details popup. Admins get an add-app tile, Edit in each popup, Organise to reorder apps and pick the What's new app, and Categories to manage categories.

A Community page card listing update emails, apps or videos, with their status and recipient counts. Admins can send or ignore pending ones, and the list is paged with a retry on error. Data comes from useAnnouncementsViewModel.
The admin-only Community page, combining subscribers, update emails, the update-email text editor and Buy Me a Coffee donations. Visitors who open the URL are sent home.

A Community page table of Buy Me a Coffee donations, showing sender, amount, message and received time, with a total count and paging. Test donations are tagged, and senders with an email get a mailto link. Data comes from useDonationsViewModel.

Admin table on the Community page listing email subscribers with confirmation status, signup date, and a delete button. Shows the total count, loading and error states, and pagination, using useSubscribersViewModel for data.

Landing page for the confirmation email link. It confirms the subscription on page load rather than through an API link, so mail scanners don't confirm it by accident. After confirming, it shows a button to subscribe to the YouTube channel.
Contact page that shows a skeleton while auth state loads. Visitors see the contact form; the signed-in admin sees the meetings calendar and the messages inbox instead.

Admin analytics dashboard with a period selector and refresh button, stat tiles, a traffic chart, and ranked lists for pages, referrers, clicks, errors, themes, devices, browsers, countries, and time zones. Ends with the visits table; data comes from useDashboardViewModel.
Admin-only route wrapper that renders the engagement Dashboard. Visitors who open the URL are sent home.
Admin view that shows the selected test feature, with pill navigation between features. Shows an empty state when no features are available, and redirects when the view model says to.
Admin-only beta route that passes the list of test features (defaulting to TEST_FEATURES) into the FeatureTesting view. Visitors who open the URL are sent home.

Admin list of raised notifications with a kind filter, sent or held status, recipients, messages, and timestamps. Includes refresh, pagination, and links to related paths; data comes from useNotificationHistoryViewModel.

Admin section titled 'On your phone' with a grouped on/off switch for each notification kind. Each row shows the 30-day count and last-sent time, and the section handles loading, error, and failure messages.
Admin-only notifications page that combines the alert channels card, the per-kind on/off settings, and the notification history. Visitors who open the URL are sent home.

Admin settings list of every external service the site connects to (Buy Me a Coffee, Cal.com, Google sign-in, hosting, ntfy), each as an expandable card. Loads settings through the settings view model and shows skeleton or error states.
Card wrapper with the 'Connections' heading that holds the list of service cards on the Settings page.
Displays a value, such as a webhook URL or redirect URI, in a code element with a copy button beside it.
Collapsible card for one external service, showing its name and status chip, with optional description, outbound links, child fields, and a test button.
Input for one setting, using a password box for secrets. It offers Save and, when a value is stored here, Remove, plus optional Generate and Copy buttons.
Admin-only Settings page that combines site visibility, signed-in devices, and the Connections list. Saved keys are stored encrypted and override server configuration.
Ordered list wrapper that presents the numbered setup instructions inside a service card.
Button that runs a connection test for a service through the test view model, showing a pending label while running and a success or error message after.

Admin Terms page that shows the terms document and lets the admin edit sections, paragraphs and bullet lists. Saving updates the date and requires visitors to accept again. Shows skeleton and error states.
Landing page for the Unsubscribe link in update emails (/updates/unsubscribe). It passes its message and back link from the updates view model into the shared UpdatesCard.
The What's New page showing the newest app or YouTube video in full, whichever came last. Shows a skeleton while loading, an error with retry, and falls back to the other item if one fails.
The YouTube page listing the author's videos newest first, nine per page, with a link to the channel and an admin-only refresh button. Each video opens on YouTube in a new tab.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/auth/authCh.text: Subscribes to sign-in and sign-out messages from other tabs in the same browser via a broadcast channel, and returns an unsubscribe function. Used by useSessionKeeper.
Broadcasts an auth message (signed in or signed out) to the browser's other tabs, excluding the current one. Listened to by the shared listeners.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/auth/useAut.text: Hook exposing the current session from the auth store slice: status, loading and authenticated flags, the user, and a signOut action. Used by many view models across pages.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/auth/useSes.text: App-wide hook that checks the session on load, extends it on user activity while signed in, signs out in the UI when it expires, and syncs sign-in and sign-out across browser tabs. Called from the app view model.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/components/.text: Hook for reordering a list by drag: mouse or pen anywhere on an item, touch only on a handle, and arrow keys on the handle. Shows the new order while dragging and calls onMove on drop.
Hook that reads the 1-based page number from the ?page URL parameter (defaulting to 1) and returns a function to change it. Used by the paged grid and the messages inbox.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/ab.text: Converts a two-letter country or region code such as RO, EU, or GB into its English display name, falling back to the uppercased code. Used by the about status editor and the Flag component.
Returns the image URL for a flag by its country code, or undefined if there is no flag or the code is unknown. Used by the Flag component in the about feature.

Maps free text containing words like 'Romanian citizenship', 'EU citizenship', or 'UK Settled Status' to a country or region code (RO, EU, GB), returning an empty string otherwise. Mirrors the API's GuessFlag logic. Used by the about status editor.

Returns the first day of the current month as a 'YYYY-MM-01' string, using the given date or now. Used by qualifications, skills, and skills chart view models, plus helpers that check upcoming status, months used, and new entries.

Extracts the last path segment of a URL and decodes it for display, so '/api/files/…/My%20CV.pdf' shows as 'My CV.pdf'. Falls back to the raw link when decoding fails. Used by the paper editor view model.
Converts a byte count to a display string in megabytes, such as '20 MB' or '24.3 MB'. Used by the about file upload view model and the apps media list editor.
Formats a 'YYYY-MM-DD' date as a short month and year (e.g. 'Jan 2023') in the viewer's locale. Used by the qualifications section view model and by formatPeriod.

Builds a date range label such as 'Jan 2020 – Mar 2022', 'Jan 2020 – Present', or 'Starting Mar 2030' for future starts. Collapses to one month when start and end match. Uses formatMonth and isUpcoming, and is used by the skills chart and item view mapping.

Checks that a URL is either an http(s) address or a path on this site, rejecting protocol-relative and javascript: links. Mirrors the API's IsSafeUrl rule and runs again before rendering links. Used across about and apps view models, and by rich text parsing and media link handling.
Returns true when a start date falls after the current month, comparing year and month only. Uses currentMonth. Used by formatPeriod and the item view mapping.

Builds a CSS background that divides the area into equal hard-edged sections, one per colour. A single colour becomes a plain fill, multiple colours become linear-gradient stripes for bars or conic-gradient slices for dots. Used by the skills chart view model.

Returns true when a licence belongs to a non-'other' category and matches an entry in OFFERED_LICENCES, meaning it appears as a toggle rather than its own row. Uses sameLicence. Used by the licences editor view model and display ordering.
Checks whether two licence entries match on category, code and name. Used by the licences editor and by the display-order and offered-status helpers in the about feature.

Immutable helper that moves an item from one index to another in an array and returns a new array. Used by reorderable list editors across the about feature, the apps dialogs, and the terms section editor.
Immutable helper that returns a copy of an array without the item at the given index. Used by most about-feature list editors, plus the categories dialog in apps.
Immutable helper that returns a copy of an array with the item at the given index swapped for a new value. Used by about-feature list editors and by the categories dialog and links editor in apps.
Sorts timeline entries newest first by end date, with ongoing entries (no end) on top and ties broken by start date, latest first. Used only by the about timeline editor.
Sorts items newest year first, keeping the original order among items from the same year. Used only by the hackathons editor in about.
Alphabetical comparison for place labels using a locale-aware collator, so accented and mixed-case names sort sensibly. Falls back to plain code-unit order on ties. Used by the places editor.

Builds a display string like 'Manchester, England, United Kingdom' from a place's name, region and country, omitting the region when it duplicates the city name. Used by the city search, place popup, places editor and world map view models.
Filters the API's validation errors down to one place in the list and strips the 'places[i].' prefix so field names match the row. Used by the places editor.
Converts a longitude and latitude in degrees into x/y coordinates on the world map's SVG box using a Natural Earth projection, with y increasing downward. Used by the world map view model.
Builds the public LeetCode profile URL for a username, URL-encoding the name. Used by the About page's LeetCode card and profile section view models.
Extracts the username from a pasted LeetCode profile link, such as leetcode.com/u/name. Any other input is returned unchanged. Used by the problem-solving editor view model.
Adds or removes a NeetCode list from a selection and returns the result in the canonical NEETCODE_LISTS order. Called by the problem-solving editor view model.
Turns an API validation key like skills[2].periods[0].uses into a readable label such as 'Skills, item 3'. Used by describeSaveError to name fields in other sections.
Converts a failed section save into field errors and a user message. Errors in other sections are listed by name, since the whole page saves together. Called by the editable section view model.
Checks whether an API error key belongs to a given section prefix, matching the prefix itself or a nested path like skills[2] or skills.x. Used by describeErrorKey and describeSaveError.
Picks the year labels for the skills chart's time axis, using a step of 1, 2, 5, or 10 years so there are at most eight labels. Used by the skills chart view model.

Computes the skills chart's time range in months, from January of the earliest skill start to the end of this year or the latest period end. Uses monthIndex and the Skill type. Called by the skills chart view model.
Formats a duration in months as text, such as '3 months', '1 year', or '6 years', rounding to whole years. Used by the skill editor and skills chart view models.
Converts a 'YYYY-MM-DD' date string into a month count since year 0, so dates can be compared and subtracted. Used by the skills chart view model, chartRange, and monthsUsed.

Returns how many months a skill has been used up to the current month, merging overlapping periods so each month counts once and future months are ignored. Used by the skills editor, skills chart, and experience sorting.
Sorts skills with the most months of use first, breaking ties alphabetically by name. Relies on monthsUsed and is called by the skills editor view model.
Builds Markdown link syntax from a label and URL, stripping square brackets from the label and falling back to the URL if the label is empty. Used by the link inserter in the about section.
Returns true for internal site paths like /contact, excluding protocol-relative URLs and /api/ paths that serve files. Used by ExternalLink to decide whether a link is local.
Splits text containing Markdown-style links into plain and linked parts, leaving links with unsafe URLs as plain text so javascript: links can't be created. Used by RichText and plainText.
Strips link syntax from text, returning only the visible labels, for example turning a link into just its label. Used for labels and sorting in papers, skills, apps, and the about page.
Creates a blank timeline entry dated to the current month with no end date, optionally including an empty bullet list. Used by the timeline editor view model.
Converts a timeline entry into the display shape the timeline shows: title, joined organization and location, upcoming flag, formatted period, and bullets. Used by the timeline section view model.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/an.text: Computes a chart axis from 0 to a round maximum split into four equal steps using 1, 2, 5, or 10 multiples. Used by the series chart view model in analytics.
Converts a two-letter country code such as GB into its English name, returning the input unchanged if it isn't a valid code. Used by the analytics dashboard view model.
Builds the one-line device label "device · browser · OS" for a visit from its device, browser and operating system fields. Used by VisitView, VisitsTable and reproductionSteps.
Turns one tracked visit event (page open, click, key, change, submit, scroll, tab switch, custom, error, leave) into a readable sentence. Used by the VisitView timeline and by reproductionSteps.
Returns the visit's starting theme, or "start → last" if the theme changed during the visit, or "unknown" when missing. Used by VisitView and reproductionSteps.
Formats a chart time bucket's start for axis labels (short) or tooltips (full). Minutes and hours use the viewer's time zone; days, months and years use UTC. Called by useSeriesChartViewModel.
Formats a number with thousands separators below 10,000, and in compact form (e.g. 12.9K) above. Used by the chart view model, RankedList and StatTiles.
Formats a number of seconds as "45s", "1m 05s" or "1h 02m". Used by StatTiles, VisitView and VisitsTable.
Formats the time since a visit started as a video-style offset such as "+0:04" or "+1:02:03". Used by VisitView and reproductionSteps.
Converts a 0–1 fraction into a rounded whole-percent string, such as 0.4167 to "42%". Used by StatTiles.

Turns a visit into plain text for pasting into an issue or AI chat: setup (device, viewport, theme, language, entry page, user agent), then timed steps with error details. Built from describeDevice, describeEvent, describeTheme and formatOffset; used by VisitView.

Browser-side recorder for a visit: queues clicks, key presses, field changes, submits, media plays, errors and page views, and sends them in batches to the analytics API. Failed batches are retried; a beacon sends the rest when the tab closes. Used by Tracker.

Returns the visible name of an element for analytics: its aria-label, then its labelled-by text, then a form field's label, name or placeholder (never its value), then its text, then an image alt or title. Used by createTracker.

Records a named analytics event with optional string details, but only for visitors. Called by the world map, media carousel, contact form, support button, subscribe dialog and token action view models.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/ap.text: Checks whether a platform is already in a list, ignoring letter case and surrounding spaces, so duplicates are caught the same way the API's AppRules catch them. Used by the platforms editor view model.
Decides whether a file to upload is a video, using its MIME type or, if the browser gives none, its file extension. Videos get the larger upload limit. Used by the media list editor view model.

Turns a pasted link into app media: a YouTube video, a video file, or an image. Returns an error message string if the link is empty or not a valid https link. Used by the media list editor view model.
Chooses the picture for an app's tile: its first image, otherwise the thumbnail of its first YouTube video, otherwise nothing. Uses the YouTube helpers and is used by the app tile view model.
Builds an embed URL for YouTube's privacy-enhanced player, which sets no cookies until a video is played. Used by the media slide and video details view models.

Extracts the 11-character video ID from a YouTube link in any common format (watch, youtu.be, shorts, embed, live), or returns null. Follows the same rules as the API. Used by the media slide, thumbnail, link and tile code.
Builds the URL of a YouTube video's high-quality thumbnail image from its ID. Used by the media slide and thumbnail view models and by tileImage.
Builds a standard YouTube watch page URL from a video ID. Used by mediaFromLink to normalize pasted YouTube links.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/co.text: Checks that a string looks like an email address and is within the maximum length. Shared by the contact form and the 'Get updates' subscribe form.
Validates the contact form's name, email, and message fields, returning an error message per field. Trims inputs and enforces required, length, and email-format rules.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/me.text: Returns the local calendar date of a given time as a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string. Used by the meetings calendar to group meetings by day.
Formats a meeting's start and end as a short, human-readable range such as 'Thu 22 Oct, 15:00–15:30' in the viewer's time zone. Used by the contact message dialog, meeting actions, and the calendar.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/si.text: React hook returning whether a given site feature is enabled, or false until the site config has loaded. Used by the contact form, the support button, and the app layout.
Fetches the public site config on mount and retries every few seconds while the API is unreachable. Called once from the app-level view model.
Returns whether a page is visible to the current viewer: always true for the signed-in admin, the site's page setting for everyone else, and null while auth or site config is still loading.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/te.text: Reads from localStorage the terms version this browser last accepted, or null if none or if storage is unavailable. Used by the terms slice.
Removes this browser's stored terms acceptance so the welcome popup appears again. Used by the development user bar's reset action.
Saves the accepted terms version to localStorage for this browser. Fails silently when storage is unavailable, so acceptance then lasts only for the current visit.

Returns the current terms' version string, its last-updated date, or 'default' if that is missing. 'unknown' means no terms are loaded. Visitors who accepted an older version are asked again when the date changes.
Fetches the site's terms once, through TermsHost, which stays mounted. Other components read the terms without subscribing, which avoids a retry loop when loading fails.

Gives view models the terms, their load state, whether the visitor accepted the current version, and whether the welcome popup should show for anonymous visitors. Also provides openTerms and reload actions. The admin sign-in page is exempt.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/up.text: Runs the confirm or unsubscribe request for the URL's token once, then reports done, error, or unknown (missing token or 404). The test token does nothing and records nothing. Success fires an analytics event.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/features/wo.text: Returns the known currency for a code. Unknown codes get a stand-in that uses the code as its name and symbol, shown after the amount.

Formats an amount with its currency symbol: whole amounts have no decimals, others have two. The symbol goes before or after the number depending on the currency. Used by the work-with-me price view model.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/layout/back.text: Watches frame timing for the Riviera background after a warm-up period. If frames average below the slow threshold over the measurement window, it calls onSlow once. Hidden tabs and long gaps restart the measurement.

Tracks the Riviera scene's time and holds it still after a period without user input. The next input resumes from the pause point, so there is no jump. It reports whether input woke a held-still scene.

Sets up the WebGL Riviera background on a canvas: compiles shaders, loads textures, and runs the render loop with idle pausing and frame-rate watching. Returns null without WebGL 2. Calls onFail if loading fails or the first frame is black.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/layout/devi.text: Decides once, before the first render, whether this device is too weak for the animated Vice theme. It checks data saver, slow connection, low memory, two or fewer cores, and missing hardware WebGL 2. storedTheme uses the result for visitors without a saved theme.

Returns 'light' or 'dark' from the device's color-scheme setting, defaulting to dark when that setting can't be read. storedTheme (terms) and reportSlowScene (meetings) use it when the visitor hasn't picked a theme.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/layout/idle.text: Sets a data-idle attribute on the page after a set period with no input, and removes it on the next input or when the window regains focus. main.tsx (site) starts it, and the returned function stops it.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/layout/mani.text: Points the page's manifest link at the admin or visitor manifest, so Add to Home Screen saves the admin app when an admin is signed in. useAppViewModel (site) calls it.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/layout/tabs.text: Reports whether a tab matches the current path, either exactly, through a nested tab's subpages, or through a group's sections. useSystemNavViewModel and useTabNavViewModel (auth) use it, and tabIndex (apps) calls it.
Gives the URL a tab links to: the first page of its group, or its own path if it isn't a group. useTabNavViewModel (auth) uses it to build tab links.
Finds the previous or next page a swipe should go to, treating groups and nested tabs as their individual pages. Returns null past either end or off a tab. useSwipeNavigation (site) uses it.
Returns a path's position in the tab order, with decimals for pages inside a group, or -1 if the path isn't a tab. usePageTransitionViewModel (apps) uses it to choose the slide direction.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/layout/them.text: Reads the visitor's saved light or dark choice from localStorage, returning null if there isn't one or storage is unavailable. storedTheme (terms) and reportSlowScene (meetings) use it.
Saves a flag in localStorage marking the device as too slow for the Vice scene, so the next visit starts in light or dark. reportSlowScene (meetings) calls it, and a blocked storage fails silently.
Saves the visitor's chosen theme to localStorage so it persists across visits. If storage is blocked, the theme still switches for the current page. listeners (shared) calls it.
Applies a theme by setting the data-theme attribute on the html element, which the glass.css styling and the analytics tracker both read. Called by the page renderer, app startup, and listeners.

Picks the starting theme: the visitor's saved choice if there is one, otherwise the system light or dark theme on slow or low-power devices, else Vice. Works even when storage is blocked, as in private windows.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/layout/useM.text: Hook that reports whether a CSS media query currently matches and re-renders when that changes. Returns false when matchMedia is unavailable. Used by useContentToggleViewModel.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/layout/useS.text: Remembers each page's scroll position per path for this tab and restores it on return, retrying as content loads until it's reached, times out, or the visitor scrolls. Used by useAppLayoutViewModel.
Builds the ordered tab list. Visitors see only enabled pages, while the signed-in admin sees all tabs with disabled ones marked hidden. Feeds the tab bar and swipe navigation.

Turns a quick, clear one-finger sideways swipe into navigation to the next or previous tab. Ignores swipes from screen edges, text fields, sideways-scrolling areas, and zoomed views. Uses useShownTabs; used by useAppLayoutViewModel.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/services/en.text: API client for the About page: a public fetch, and an admin-only update that replaces the whole page and returns it trimmed, with validation errors keyed by field path. Used by aboutApi.

API client for visit analytics. Public calls send event batches, including a beacon variant for closing tabs. Admin-only calls fetch the summary, session list and details, and delete sessions. Used by analyticsApi.

API client for the apps catalogue. Public calls list apps, categories, and the What's new app. Admin-only calls create, update, and delete apps, and save the display order and categories. Used by appsApi.

API client for sign-in. Gets the current user, logs out this device, and builds the Google sign-in URL. Admin-only calls list signed-in devices and end one or all other sessions. Used by several auth and admin modules.
Client calls for the contact form and admin inbox: public send, admin list, read, mark-as-read, delete, and email reply to a sender. Talks to /api/contact endpoints.
Admin upload calls for photos (JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF up to 15 MB), academic papers (PDF up to 200 MB), and app media (images or MP4/MOV/WebM video). Used by the media list editor in apps.
Public call that fetches LeetCode stats for the user set on the About Me page, returning null when none is set. Used by aboutApi; errors cover unknown user (404) and unreachable service (503).

Admin calls for meetings booked through Cal.com: get the booking page URL, list meetings in a date range, accept or decline a request with a message, and cancel an accepted meeting. Used by meetingsApi.

Admin calls for alert settings: list and toggle notification kinds and delivery channels, manage push-notification devices (add, remove, test), and page through sent notifications. Used by notificationsApi.
Admin city search that returns cities matching a typed name, largest first, with optional region or country narrowing. Used by aboutApi.
Public call that returns the site owner's first name from /api/firstname. No callers are listed in the map.
Résumé calls: public PDF and headline URLs, admin settings, saving contact details and section choices, and generating both PDF versions (with and without phone). Used by resumeApi.
Admin calls to read and save app settings by key, and to run test checks for ntfy alerts, email, YouTube, and the Cal.com key. Used by settingsApi.
Site-wide status: public read of which pages and features are visible and whether maintenance mode is on, plus an admin partial update. Used by fetchSite and saveSite.

Maps a Buy Me a Coffee event type to a short label such as "refunded" or "membership started". Plain coffee purchases and one-off donations return null, and unknown types pass through unchanged. Used by the Donations view.

API client for support. get() fetches the public Buy Me a Coffee link for the header button, and listDonations() fetches the admin's paginated donation list, newest first. Used by the updates API module.

API client for the terms page. get() fetches the public terms document, which returns defaults until an admin first saves. update() lets an admin replace the terms and returns the stored version or path-keyed validation errors. Used by the terms API module.

API client for the email updates feature. Public calls handle subscribing, confirming, and unsubscribing via email links. Admin calls manage subscribers, announcements (send or ignore), and the update email wording, including previews and test sends. Used by the updates API module.

API client for the Work With Me price. getPrice() returns the public price, defaulting to €25 until an admin saves one. savePrice() lets an admin update it and returns field errors on invalid currency or amount. Used by the workWithMe API module.

API client for YouTube data. channel() returns the site owner's channel, or null when none is set. listVideos() returns a paginated public video list. refreshVideos() lets an admin force a fresh pull from YouTube and returns the video count. Used by the apps API module.

frontend:symbol:frontend/src/services/ht.text: Error class for failed HTTP requests, carrying status, request description, field validation errors, and problem details. Status is 0 for network failures. Used by the auth, analytics, site, and shared failure-mapping code.
